| `supports_deeplinking` | boolean | Null when unknown. |

post.description: Find retailers and brands across affiliate networks by name or domain, and see which network carries them, how many products they list, their categories and countries, and link templates to fill with your own publisher ID.

search.description: Case-insensitive fragment of the merchant name or home_url, for example `Walmart` or `walmart.com`. Does not match IDs.

network_ids.description: Comma-separated numeric network IDs, as in a merchant's `network.id`.

origin_ids.description: Comma-separated merchant IDs as the source network assigns them.

category_name.description:
Category name filter.

Provider reference: maximum 255.

countries.description: Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the merchant operates in, for example `US,CA`.

countries_origin.description: Comma-separated codes for the merchant's origin country.

countries_market.description: Comma-separated codes for the merchant's market countries.

feed_languages.description: Comma-separated ISO 639-1 codes of the product feed.

product_count_min.description:
Only merchants with at least this many products.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

product_count_max.description:
Only merchants with at most this many products.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

promotion_count_min.description:
Only merchants with at least this many promotions.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

promotion_count_max.description:
Only merchants with at most this many promotions.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

has_commissionable_url.description:
`1` keeps only merchants with a stored commissionable URL template. Not a test for linkability: read providers[].template instead.

Provider reference: allowed values ["1"].

per_page.description:
Merchants per page, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10 here; merchant records are large.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50.

page.description:
Page number, starting at 1.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

fields.description: Comma-separated field names to keep in each record, for example `id,name,logo_url`. Omit for every field.

200.description:
One network under `data`, with description, links and created/updated timestamps when the API sends them. Upstream has served that record both as a single object (live, 2026-10-14) and as a one-element array (the reference page). This returns the object either way. | `logo_url` | string |  |
| `merchant_count` | number | Merchants on this network. |

200.description:

| `id` | number | Numeric network ID; pass to networks/get or as a merchants/search network_ids filter. |
| `object_id` | string | Stable `rnet_` identifier of this regional network. |
| `slug` | string | Short `rnet_` slug. |
| `name` | string | Regional network name, for example `Impact Australia`. |
| `url` | string | Network homepage. |
| `logo_url` | string |  |
| `merchant_count` | number | Merchants on this network. |
| `merchant_count_active` | number | Merchants currently active. |
| `product_count` | number | Products indexed for this network. |
| `promotion_count` | number |  |
| `record_types` | string[] | What the network carries, for example `products`. |
| `merchant_network_types` | string[] | `standard` or `asn` (Amazon Seller Network). |
| `canonical_id` | string | `net_` ID of the platform the regional network belongs to. |
| `countries` | string[] | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes. Present on the 2026-10-14 responses. |
| `group` | object | Parent platform brand (`id`, `name`). Shown on the reference page; absent from the 2026-10-14 rows. |
| `country` | object | Country object (`id`, `iso3`, `name`). Shown on the reference page; the 2026-10-14 rows used `countries` instead. |

post.description: Search affiliate product listings by keyword, identifier, price, brand, merchant or network.

keyword.description: Plain-text search such as `JBL speaker`; sent as the string form of `search`.

search.description:
Filter objects `{ field, value, operator }`, ANDed together. Fields include any, name, brand, category, barcode, sku, asin, merchant.id, network.id, final_price, currency, availability, on_sale, merchant.countries. Operators: =, !=, LIKE, NOT LIKE, >, <, >=, <=, NOT NULL. `||` in value ORs values.

Provider reference: maximum 30.

query.description: Rule builder `{ rules_operator: any|all, rules: [{ conditions_operator, conditions: [{ field, operator, value }] }] }`. Exclusive with keyword and search.

per_page.description:
Products per page, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10 here.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50.

page.description:
Page number, starting at 1.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

after.description: Deep-pagination cursor from the previous response's meta.after, for results past 10,000 on plans that allow it.

exact_total.description: Count meta.total past 10,000 precisely, at some extra latency.

fields.description:
Product fields to return, for example `id`, `name`, `final_price`, `urls`.

Provider reference: maximum 50.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction.

Provider reference: allowed values ["asc", "desc"].

duplicate_fields_to_exclude.description: Deduplicate by name, image_url, direct_url, barcode or merchant.id. Comma syntax applies each independently and accepts `[N]` caps (`name,merchant.id[10]`); `a||b` drops a row when either has appeared.

facets.description:
Aggregations to include: network, merchant, final_price, or dotted sub-fields such as network.name.

Provider reference: maximum 20.

sort_by.description:
Sort field: relevance, id, barcode, ean, gtin, upc, isbn, asin, name, currency, regular_price, final_price, sale_discount, stock_quantity, commissionable_status, brand, category, color, gender, size, author, network.id, network.name, merchant.id, merchant.name, added_at, updated_at.

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "id", "barcode", "ean", "gtin", "upc", "isbn", "asin", "name", "currency", "regular_price", "final_price", "sale_discount", "stock_quantity", "commissionable_status", "brand", "category", "color", "gender", "size", "author", "network.id", "network.name", "merchant.id", "merchant.name", "added_at", "updated_at"].

balanced_mix.description: `{ field, max_per_value, interleave?, weights? }` to keep one merchant or brand from dominating. Not combinable with duplicate_fields_to_exclude.

post.description: Get the featured buy-box offer for one Amazon.nl ASIN or product URL: EUR price, list price and discount, stock state and text, seller and shipper, delivery promise and the other-offers summary. Set include_other_offers to also read the first page of other sellers' offers from the public all-offers drawer.

asin.description: Amazon.nl ASIN, or ISBN-10 for books. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{10}$.

include_other_offers.description: Also fetch the first page (up to 10) of other sellers' offers. One extra request.

url.description: HTTPS amazon.nl /dp/ASIN or /gp/product/ASIN URL. Supply this or asin. Pattern: ^https://(?:www\.)?amazon\.nl/(?:[^?#]*/)?(?:dp|gp/product)/[A-Za-z0-9]{10}(?:[/?#]|$).

200.description:
Get the featured buy-box offer for one Amazon.nl ASIN or product URL: EUR price, list price and discount, stock state and text, seller and shipper, delivery promise and the other-offers summary. Set include_other_offers to also read the first page of other sellers' offers from the public all-offers drawer.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `asin` | string | ASIN of the listing Amazon.nl shows; differs from requested_asin when Amazon merged or retired the requested listing. |
| `asin_redirected` | boolean | True when Amazon.nl answered the requested ASIN with another listing (merged or retired ASIN); asin and every other field then describe the shown listing. |
| `availability_text` | string | Stock text as displayed, for example 'Op voorraad', 'Nog maar 3 op voorraad' or 'Tijdelijk niet op voorraad.'. |
| `country` | string |  |
| `delivery_date_text` | string |  |
| `delivery_price_text` | string |  |
| `delivery_text` | string |  |
| `fulfilled_by_amazon` | boolean |  |
| `in_stock` | boolean | Parsed from availability_text; null when the text is absent or unrecognized. |
| `list_price` | object | Displayed EUR price. display is normalized to '€ 1.234,56'; amount is the parsed number (1234.56). All three are null when the page shows no price. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `offer_state` | string |  |
| `other_offers` | object | Null unless include_other_offers is true. |
| `other_offers_text` | string | The page's other-offers summary ('Nieuw en gebruikt (N) van ...'), when shown. |
| `price` | object | Displayed EUR price. display is normalized to '€ 1.234,56'; amount is the parsed number (1234.56). All three are null when the page shows no price. |
| `requested_asin` | string | The ASIN taken from the input asin or url. |
| `savings_percent` | number | Displayed discount percentage, when Amazon shows one. |
| `secondary_delivery_text` | string |  |
| `seller` | string | Buy-box seller ('Verkocht door'), for example 'Amazon'. |
| `seller_id` | string | Merchant id of a third-party seller; null for Amazon. |
| `ships_from` | string | Buy-box shipper ('Verzonden door'). Equals seller when Amazon renders the merged 'Verzender / Verkoper' row. |
| `sold_by_amazon` | boolean |  |
| `title` | string |  |
| `url` | string |  |

features: MAAK KENNIS MET ALEXA: Echo Dot is een smartspeaker met spraakbesturing die verbonden kan worden met Alexa om muziek af te spelen, timers en wekkers in te stellen, vragen te stellen, je huis slimmer te maken met compatibele apparaten en nog veel meer. Het enige wat je moet doen, is het vragen. Beschikbaar in het Nederlands.
KRACHTIGE SOUND, KLEIN FORMAAT: Onze bestseller Echo met heldere klanken, diepe bas en een vol geluid in elke ruimte.

MUZIEK BEDIENEN MET JE STEM: Vraag Alexa om muziek en podcasts af te spelen vanaf je favoriete aanbieders zoals Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify en luister naar radiostations. Koppel je smartphone via bluetooth en stream door je hele ruimte.
ALEXA HELPT JE GRAAG: Vraag Alexa naar het weerbericht, om handsfree timers in te stellen, naar een antwoord op je vragen en zelfs om moppen te vertellen.

MAAK HET JE MAKKELIJK IN HUIS: Bedien compatibele smarthome-apparaten met je stem of met routines die geactiveerd worden door binnentemperatuursensoren. Je kunt routines instellen om slimme ventilatoren automatisch in te schakelen als de binnentemperatuur hoger is dan de door jou ingestelde omgevingstemperatuur.
ONTWORPEN OM JE PRIVACY TE BESCHERMEN: Meerdere lagen privacybescherming, waaronder een Microfoon uit-knop die de microfoons elektronisch uitschakelt.

BESCHIKBAARHEID VAN FUNCTIES: Alexa wordt altijd slimmer en krijgt steeds meer nieuwe functies en skills. Selecteer Nederlands in de Alexa-app om toegang te krijgen tot lokale Nederlandse functies en skills.

ONTWORPEN VOOR DUURZAAMHEID: 99% van de verpakking is afkomstig uit verantwoordelijk beheerde bossen of van gerecyclede grondstoffen, gebruik van 95% gerecyclede stof en 55% gerecycled plastic na gebruik.

specifications.name: Gewicht
specifications.value: 340 gr Werkelijke grootte en gewicht kunnen variëren door productieproces.

specifications.name: Wifi-connectiviteit
specifications.value: Wifi vereist. Dual-band wifi ondersteunt 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac (2,4 en 5 GHz) netwerken. Ondersteunt geen verbinding met ad-hoc- (of peer-to-peer-) wifi-netwerken.

specifications.name: Bluetooth-connectiviteit
specifications.value: A2DP-ondersteuning (Advanced Audio Distribution Profile) voor audiostreaming van je mobiele apparaat naar Echo Dot of van Echo Dot naar je Bluetooth-luidspreker. AVRCP (Audio/Video Remote Control Profile) voor spraakbesturing van aangesloten mobiele apparaten. Handsfree spraakbesturing wordt niet ondersteund voor Mac OS X-apparaten. Bluetooth-luidsprekers waarvoor pincodes zijn vereist, worden niet ondersteund.

specifications.name: Systeemvereisten
specifications.value: Echo Dot is klaar om verbinding te maken met je wifi. De Alexa-app is geschikt voor Fire OS-, Android- en iOS-apparaten en is ook toegankelijk via je webbrowser. Ondersteunde besturingssystemen. Bepaalde skills en diensten kunnen een abonnement vereisen of andere kosten met zich meebrengen.

specifications.name: Configuratietechnologie
specifications.value: Met de eenvoudige wifi-configuratie van Amazon kunnen klanten in enkele eenvoudige stappen slimme apparaten verbinden met hun wifi-netwerk. De eenvoudige wifi-configuratie is nogmaals een manier waarop Alexa steeds slimmer wordt.

specifications.name: Garantie en service
specifications.value: Amazon Echo Dot (5e generatie) wordt verkocht met een beperkte garantie van één jaar die door de fabrikant wordt verstrekt. Als je consument bent, is de beperkte garantie een aanvulling op je consumentenrechten en die brengt deze rechten op geen enkele wijze in gevaar. Dit betekent dat je nog steeds aanvullende rechten hebt, zelfs nadat de beperkte garantie is verlopen ( klik hier voor meer informatie over je consumentenrechten). Het gebruik van Amazon Echo Dot is onderworpen aan de voorwaarden die hier worden gevonden.

specifications.name: Toegankelijkheidsfuncties
specifications.value: De Alexa-app en producten die geschikt zijn voor Alexa bevatten verschillende functies voor klanten met toegankelijkheidsbehoeften op het gebied van zicht, gehoor, mobiliteit en spraak. Vind hier meer informatie over Alexa-toegankelijkheid.

specifications.name: Wat zit er in de doos
specifications.value: Echo Dot (5e generatie) Antraciet, netadapter (15 W) en snelstartgids.

specifications.name: Privacyfuncties
specifications.value: Activeringswoord-technologie, streamingindicatoren, Microfoon Uit-knop, de mogelijkheid om je spraakopnames te bekijken en te verwijderen en meer. Bezoek de pagina Alexa, Echo-apparaten en jouw Privacy om te ontdekken hoe Alexa- en Echo-apparaten zijn ontworpen om jouw privacy te beschermen.

specifications.name: Talen
specifications.value: Alexa spreekt Nederlands, Engels, Duits, Frans, Italiaans en Spaans (aanbevolen taal voor toegang tot Skills: Nederlands)

specifications.name: Alexa-skills en -functies
specifications.value: Alexa maakt je leven gemakkelijker, zinvoller en leuker door je met je stem je wereld te laten bedienen. Alexa kan je helpen meer te halen uit de dingen waar je al van houdt en nieuwe mogelijkheden te ontdekken waar je nooit aan hebt gedacht.

top_reviews.author: Luc Wijdeveld
top_reviews.text: Kocht het als toevoeging van mijn Eufy video deurbel. Kende het wel, maar had al eerder terug gestuurd omdat ik er niks mee kon. Nu kan ik er wel wat mee, Alexa verteld mij als er iemand aanbelt, als ik de bel niet heb gehoord. 's Morgens roep ik dan: "Alexa, goedemorgen" en je krijgt de noviteit van de dag. Verder doe ik er niets mee, wie weet komt dat later, ben niet van abonnementen.
top_reviews.title: Gekocht als toevoeging op mijn Eufy video deurbel.

top_reviews.author: Fran
top_reviews.text:
Aaw, ik wilde twee Echo Dots (5e generatie) cadeau geven aan mijn zoons. Omdat ik zelf totaal geen ervaring had met slimme speakers en niet wist of het wel écht leuk zou zijn, heb ik besloten er drie te kopen: twee als cadeau en één voor mijzelf. Dankzij de Black Friday-deals was de prijs bovendien heel aantrekkelijk.
Inmiddels heb ik mijn eigen Echo Dot uitgebreid getest (witte uitvoering) en die staat nu standaard in mijn studio. En eerlijk is eerlijk: ik ben verkocht.
Uiterlijk
De Echo Dot heeft een strak, modern ontwerp met slechts vier knoppen bovenop. De kleur ‘wit’ is eigenlijk een mooie zachtgrijze tint, wat ik persoonlijk juist erg mooi vind. Hij oogt rustig en past perfect in mijn interieur.
Geluid
Wat een verrassing! Het geluid is echt beter dan ik had verwacht. Voor de ruimte waarin ik hem gebruik is het volume meer dan voldoende, en zelfs op laag volume klinkt de muziek vol en warm. De bas is verrassend goed voor zo’n compact apparaat.
Gebruik
Ik gebruik geen slimme apparaten, dus daar kan ik niets over zeggen. Maar wat ik wél gebruik, doe ik inmiddels dagelijks: muziek via Spotify, nieuwsflitsen (NOS), het weerbericht, reminders, boodschappenlijstjes, timers en het opzoeken van feitjes.
Muziek bedienen met je stem werkt fantastisch. Ik vraag Alexa om favoriete nummers of afspeellijsten en regel het volume zonder ook maar iets aan te raken. Het weerbericht gebruik ik meerdere keren per dag: van een uitgebreid overzicht tot even snel checken of het het komende uur gaat regenen – zó handig.
Reminders zijn voor mij een enorme plus. In plaats van notities op mijn telefoon vertel ik alles aan Alexa. Ze herinnert me aan spullen die ik moet meenemen naar afspraken en laat me weten wanneer het tijd is om te vertrekken. Mijn boodschappenlijst vul ik tussendoor gewoon aan met mijn stem.
De timerfunctie gebruik ik niet alleen in de keuken, maar ook voor mijn werk. Bijvoorbeeld bij het bedrukken van T-shirts: 30 seconden persen? Alexa houdt het bij en ik heb mijn handen vrij. Ideaal.
En dan nog dit: ik speel graag woordspelletjes en kom daarbij regelmatig lastige woorden tegen. Waar ik vroeger Google gebruikte, vraag ik het nu gewoon aan Alexa. Ze geeft snel en duidelijk uitleg. Heerlijk gemak.
Conclusie
De cadeaus worden over twee weken gegeven en als mijn zoons hier net zo enthousiast over zijn als ik, dan zit het helemaal goed. Ik kan dit product van harte aanbevelen. De Echo Dot is niet alleen praktisch en handig, maar ook verrassend leuk en gezellig in huis. Een aankoop waar ik echt blij van word!
top_reviews.title: Blij verrast – nu al fan van de Echo Dot (5e generatie)!

top_reviews.title: Surprising sound and fast responses

top_reviews.author: prime reviewer
top_reviews.text:
If you’ve ever wanted a tiny, round friend who can answer your questions, play your favorite tunes, and occasionally judge your life choices, then the Alexa Dot Echo 2022 is your new best buddy!
First off, let’s talk about the size. This little gadget is so compact that it could easily be mistaken for a fancy coaster. I mean, if you ever need to impress someone with your “high-tech” decor, just place it next to your coffee mug and watch the confusion unfold. “Is that a speaker or a really advanced drink holder?”
Now, onto the voice recognition. Alexa is like that friend who always thinks they know what you’re talking about, even when they don’t. You could ask her to play “Bohemian Rhapsody,” and she might just start reciting the ingredients for a lasagna. But hey, who doesn’t love a surprise cooking lesson while trying to rock out?
And let’s not forget the smart home integration. You can control your lights, thermostat, and even your coffee maker with just your voice. Just be careful not to accidentally summon the vacuum cleaner while you’re still in your pajamas. Nothing says “I’m not ready for adulting” like a Roomba chasing you around the living room.
The sound quality? Well, let’s just say it’s like listening to your favorite band through a tin can. But hey, if you’re not too picky, it’s perfect for drowning out the sound of your neighbor’s questionable taste in music.
In conclusion, the Alexa Dot Echo 2022 is the perfect blend of convenience and comedy. It’s like having a personal assistant who’s also a stand-up comedian—just don’t expect her to get your jokes. If you’re looking for a device that can do it all while keeping you entertained, this little orb is worth every penny. Just remember to keep your questions simple, or you might end up with a lasagna recipe instead of your favorite song!
top_reviews.title: absolutely! especially during prime day deals

top_reviews.author: Suresh Kumar
top_reviews.text:
I recently purchased the Alexa Dot 5th Generation, and I must say, it has exceeded my expectations in every way. Here's a detailed breakdown of my experience:
Design & Build:
The compact and sleek design is perfect for any room. The rounded edges and fabric finish give it a modern, elegant look that blends seamlessly with my decor. It’s lightweight yet feels sturdy.
Sound Quality:
The improvement in audio quality is remarkable compared to earlier models. The sound is clearer, bass is deeper, and it fills the room nicely for such a small device. Whether I'm listening to music, podcasts, or setting alarms, the audio does not disappoint.
Smart Features:
Alexa's capabilities have impressed me time and again. From controlling smart home devices (lights, thermostat, and even my TV) to providing quick answers and weather updates, it has become an indispensable part of my daily routine. The integration with third-party apps like Spotify works seamlessly.
I am enjoying the drop in feature very much.
Enhanced Features:
The addition of motion detection and temperature sensing in the 5th Generation is a game-changer. For example, the motion detection feature turns on my lights automatically when I enter the room, and the temperature sensor helps me adjust my thermostat smartly.
Ease of Use:
Setting it up was a breeze. The Alexa app walks you through the process step by step, making it beginner-friendly. Voice recognition is top-notch—it even distinguishes between different family members!
Room for Improvement:
While it's an excellent device, I noticed that the microphone sensitivity could sometimes be a bit too high, picking up commands from other rooms (im having one in each room). Also, it would be great to have a USB-C charging option instead of the proprietary adapter (If so we can play with longer cable or shorter cable where needed).
Overall Verdict:
The Alexa Dot 5th Generation is a fantastic upgrade with thoughtful features and improvements. It’s versatile, user-friendly, and truly enhances the smart home experience. Whether you're a first-time Alexa user or upgrading from an earlier model, I highly recommend it!
top_reviews.title: A Smart Assistant Packed with Impressive Features!

post.description: To find FCC equipment authorization filings by grantee, applicant, date range or technical filters; use lookup_fcc_id for one exact FCC ID.

applicant_name.description: Applicant / grantee name (the site matches a prefix).

application_purpose.description:
I = Change in FCC ID, P = Class II Permissive Change, S = Class III Permissive Change, O = Original Grant.

Provider reference: allowed values ["I", "P", "S", "O"].

application_status.description:
granted (default: all granted statuses), all (grants, dismissals and denials), GI (grant issued), IP (permissive change issued), IM (modification of FCC ID issued), DM (dismissed), DN (denied).

Provider reference: allowed values ["granted", "all", "GI", "IP", "IM", "DM", "DN"].

cursor.description: Continuation from a previous page (meta.page.next_cursor): the site's 1-based FromRec offset of the next page.

equipment_class.description: Numeric equipment class code from the site's search form select (e.g. 103 = DTS Digital Transmission System). Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,4}$.

final_action_date_from.description: Earliest final action (grant) date, YYYY-MM-DD. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

final_action_date_to.description: Latest final action (grant) date, YYYY-MM-DD. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

grantee_code.description: Grantee code (3 or 5 characters), e.g. IPH.

lower_frequency_mhz.description:
Lower frequency filter in MHz.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

modular_type.description:
1 single modular, 2 limited single modular, 3 split modular, 4 limited split modular approval.

Provider reference: allowed values ["1", "2", "3", "4"].

page_size.description:
Rows per page (the form's show_records; 500 accepted by the site).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 500; default 25.

product_code.description: Product code (the FCC ID after the grantee code, hyphen included), up to 14 characters; prefix match unless product_exact_match.

product_exact_match.description: Match product_code exactly instead of as a prefix.

rule_parts.description: Up to 3 FCC rule parts as the form lists them (e.g. 15C, 22H, 90).

tcb_code.description: Telecommunication Certification Body code, e.g. US0101.

tcb_scope.description: TCB scope code A1..A4, B1..B4. Pattern: ^[AB][1-4]$.

upper_frequency_mhz.description:
Upper frequency filter in MHz.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

post.description: Deposit market share: how much each bank holds in a city, county, state or MSA, or where one bank's deposits sit. Filter by `cert`, `year`, branch `state` and `city`, or by any column with `filters` (`CNTYNAMB`, `MSABR`, `ZIPBR`).

cert.description:
FDIC certificate number, the institution id shared by every BankFind dataset (3511 = Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.; 628 = JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.). Find it with `institutions`. A number no institution has ever held is not_found.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 9999999.

city.description: Exact city, matched against `CITYBR` as BankFind stores it, case included (`Sioux Falls`, not `sioux falls`). Pattern: ^[^"\\]+$.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page of the same query (the record offset).

fields.description: Projection: column names to return instead of the default set, e.g. ["NAMEBR", "CITYBR", "DEPSUMBR", "ASSET"]. The identity columns are always added and every record carries `ID`. An unknown name is ignored. The FDIC's column definitions are at https://api.fdic.gov/banks/docs/.

filters.description: Raw BankFind filter, ANDed with the other inputs. Lucene-style: `FIELD:value`, `FIELD:"two words"`, `FIELD:("A","B")` for any of several, `FIELD:[low TO high]` for an inclusive range (`*` open), `!(FIELD:value)` to exclude, `AND`/`OR` between terms. Column names are upper case and values match exactly as stored, case included. An unknown column matches nothing (an empty result, not an error); a syntax error is invalid_input.

from_year.description:
Earliest survey year to include.

Provider reference: minimum 1934; maximum 2100.

page_size.description:
Records per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000; default 25.

sort_by.description: Columns to sort by, in priority order, e.g. ["DEPSUMBR"]. Defaults to `YEAR` then `DEPSUMBR`, descending. Unique tiebreak columns are always appended so offset paging is stable. An unsortable or unknown column is invalid_input.

sort_order.description:
Direction for every sort column. Defaults to the direction of the default sort.

Provider reference: allowed values ["asc", "desc"].

state.description: Two-letter state or territory code, matched against `STALPBR`, the branch's state. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2,3}$.

to_year.description:
Latest survey year to include.

Provider reference: minimum 1934; maximum 2100.

year.description:
One survey year (deposits as of June 30), 1994 onward. Not combinable with `from_year` / `to_year`.

Provider reference: minimum 1934; maximum 2100.

post.description: Page through all customer reviews of one Best Buy US product (SKU or product/review URL), 20 per source page, via the endpoint Best Buy's own review pages call. Each review: stable review_id, 1-5 rating, title, text, author display name, submitted_at (ISO 8601), verified_purchase, incentivized, recommended, helpful/unhelpful votes, pros/cons, attribute ratings, photo URLs and the purchased variant. Also total_reviews, average_rating and the 1-5 star rating_distribution. sort: newest (default), oldest, most_helpful, highest, lowest, relevant. Pass next_cursor back as cursor until it is null to read every review (pages=1-10 fetches that many source pages per call). Incremental sync: sort=newest and stop at the first review_id or submitted_at already stored; for a backfill under live writes prefer sort=oldest, whose offsets do not shift when new reviews arrive.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous call for the same product and sort. Omit for the first page.

pages.description:
Source pages (20 reviews each) to fetch in this call; 1 when omitted.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 10.

sku.description: Best Buy SKU, the same id the other functions take. Supply this or url. Pattern: ^[0-9]{6,8}$.

sort.description:
Review order; newest when omitted. Must match the sort of a supplied cursor.

Provider reference: allowed values ["newest", "oldest", "most_helpful", "highest", "lowest", "relevant"].

url.description: https://www.bestbuy.com product or reviews URL carrying the SKU (skuId query or the numeric path segment). Supply this or sku.

value.abstract_en: A negative electrode of a lithium secondary battery having a mixture layer containing graphite particles and an organic binder on a current collector, wherein the diffraction intensity ratio (002)/(110) of the mixture layer measured by X-ray diffraction is not higher than 500, and a lithium secondary battery having that negative electrode and a positive electrode containing a lithium compound. Since the quick charge/discharge characteristics and the cycle characteristics do not deteriorate significantly when the negative electrode density of the lithium secondary battery is increased, a high- capacity lithium secondary battery having an enhanced energy density per volume of secondary battery can be provided.
value.abstract_fr: La présente invention a trait à une électrode négative pour un accumulateur au lithium comportant une couche de mélange contenant des particules de graphite et un liant organique sur un collecteur de courant, dans laquelle le rapport d'intensité de diffraction (002)/(110) de la couche de mélange mesurée par diffraction de rayons X est égale ou inférieure à 500, et un accumulateur au lithium comportant cette électrode négative et une électrode positive contenant un composé de lithium. Etant donné que les caractéristiques de charge/décharge rapide et les caractéristiques de cycle ne se détériorent pas de manière significative lors de l'accroissement de la densité d'électrode négative de l'accumulateur au lithium, il est possible d'obtenir un accumulateur au lithium haute capacité présentant une densité d'énergie améliorée par volume d'un accumulateur au lithium.

post.description: Start here to find patent numbers by keyword, title, inventor, applicant or owner name, IPC class, PCT or international publication number, or a date range; then call get_patent with a returned patent_number.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page (the zero-based offset of the next hit). Keep every other input identical. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,5}$.

date_type.description:
Which date the `from_date`/`to_date` range applies to. Requires both dates.

Provider reference: allowed values ["issue-date", "filing-date", "exam-request-date", "publication-date", "priority-date", "national-entry-date", "green-technology-granted-date"].

field.description:
Restrict `query` to one bibliographic field (the CPD advanced-search field list). `intl-number` is the WO international publication number, `pct-number` the PCT filing number.

Provider reference: allowed values ["title", "abstract", "claims", "description", "inventor", "applicant", "current-owner", "owners-on-record", "ipc", "pct-number", "intl-number"].

from_date.description: Inclusive range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Requires `date_type` and `to_date`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

language.description:
Interface language of the results (English or French titles and summary URLs). The query syntax is the same in both.

Provider reference: allowed values ["en", "fr"]; default "en".

page_size.description:
Hits per page (the site serves 10, 25, 50 and 100; any value up to 100 is accepted).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 10.

query.description: Search words, or a raw CPD query expression (`field:(words)`, AND/OR/NOT, `date-field:[YYYY-MM-DD TO YYYY-MM-DD]`). Combined with `field`, only plain words belong here.

search_type.description:
CPD search mode. Default: `basic` for plain words, `advanced` as soon as `field` or a date range is given. Pass `advanced` or `boolean` yourself when `query` is already a fielded expression.

Provider reference: allowed values ["basic", "advanced", "boolean"].

to_date.description: Inclusive range end, YYYY-MM-DD. Requires `date_type` and `from_date`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

200.description:
Search the Canadian Patents Database. Free-text keyword search by default; set `field` to restrict the query to one bibliographic field (title, abstract, claims, inventor, applicant, current-owner, ipc, pct-number, ...), or give a raw CPD query expression such as `title:(solar panel) AND (issue-date:[2020-01-01 TO 2025-12-31])` with `search_type` advanced or boolean. Returns one page of ranked hits (patent number, title, relevance score, summary URL) with the total count and a `next_cursor` for the following page. The site displays at most 5,000 hits per query (`display_limit_exceeded`); narrow broad queries with a date range.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `patent_number` | string | CA patent or application number; the key for get_patent. |
| `rank` | number | 1-based position in the full result list. |
| `score_percent` | number | Relevance score as shown (`98%` -> 98); null when not shown. |
| `source_url` | string | Patent summary page URL. |
| `title` | string | Title in the interface language; null when the site shows no title in that language (older records in the French interface). |

THIS... is a 2023 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS Weissach Package, finished in paint-to-sample Maritime Blue with a black and blue interior.
- The odometer on this Cayman GT4 RS currently displays approximately 6,500 miles.
- This Porsche is offered with a clean `Carfax` vehicle history report.
- A partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes the Weissach and Sport Chrono packages, a front-axle lift system, Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes (PCCB), and a Bose sound system. The seller reports no notable modifications.
- Introduced in 2022, the Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS boasts a naturally aspirated 4.0-liter flat-6 engine derived from the 911 GT3, featuring a 9,000-rpm redline, six individual throttle bodies, and a carbon fiber airbox mounted directly behind the driver and passenger. The sole transmission choice is a 7-speed PDK with shortened gear ratios compared to the standard GT4.
- Power comes from a 4.0-liter flat-6, rated at 493 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission.

post.description: Find solicitations by keyword (description; with `match: any` also item description, bid number and alternate id), organization (agency), buyer, NIGP class, type code, status, UNSPSC category or opening-date window; pass a row's `bid_number` to get_bid and a `blanket_number` to get_blanket. Use list_open_bids instead for the site's curated list of currently open solicitations. At least one criterion is required; a legitimate zero-row answer sets `total_count` to 0.

bid_number.description: Bid solicitation number or prefix, e.g. `BD-27-1060-ITD00-ITD00-133949` or `BD-27-1060` (the form's Bid # field).

buyer.description: Buyer id as the site uses it (e.g. `AUDREY.BANKS`) or the buyer's name as listed (`Last, First`); a unique fragment is accepted.

category_code.description: UNSPSC segment of the form's Category dropdown: the two-digit code, e.g. `43` (Information Technology Broadcasting and Telecommunications) or `00` (Grants), or a unique fragment of its name.

cursor.description: Row offset of the page to return (a multiple of 25), as given by the previous answer's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page. The same criteria must be passed again; the site's session is re-established on every call. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,6}$.

keyword.description: Free text matched against the solicitation description (the form's Description field). With `match: any` it is also applied to the item description, bid number and alternate id, as the site's quick search does.

match.description:
`all` (default): every filled criterion must match (the form's default). `any`: the site's Any/OR switch; the keyword is copied into the description, item description, bid number and alternate id fields, and a row matches when ANY filled criterion matches - so combining `any` with `status` or `type_code` returns every bid with that status or type, not the intersection. Use `any` for keyword-only quick searches and `all` when combining filters.

Provider reference: allowed values ["all", "any"]; default "all".

nigp_class.description: NIGP class code of the form's NIGP Class dropdown, e.g. `43-23`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

opening_date_from.description: Bid opening date lower bound as the form takes it, MM/DD/YYYY. Pattern: ^(0[1-9]|1[0-2])/(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])/[0-9]{4}$.

opening_date_to.description: Bid opening date upper bound, MM/DD/YYYY. Pattern: ^(0[1-9]|1[0-2])/(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])/[0-9]{4}$.

organization.description: Organization (agency) code as the site uses it, e.g. `1060`, or its name as listed, e.g. `Executive Office of Technology Services and Security`; a unique case-insensitive fragment of the name is accepted, an ambiguous one is rejected with candidates.

status.description:
Status code: 2BA Approved, 2BCL Closed, 2BE Evaluated, 2BIA Intent To Award, 2BO Opened, 2BPO Bid to PO, 2BS Sent (open for responses).

Provider reference: allowed values ["2BA", "2BCL", "2BE", "2BIA", "2BO", "2BPO", "2BS"].

type_code.description:
Solicitation type: NS Non-Statewide Solicitation, SH Historical Solicitation, SS Statewide Solicitation.

Provider reference: allowed values ["NS", "SH", "SS"].

200.description:
Recorded ACRIS real-property documents (deeds, mortgages, agreements, liens, ...) against one tax lot, from NYC Open Data: ACRIS Real Property Legals (8h5j-fqxa) filtered by borough/block/lot gives the document ids, then ACRIS Real Property Master (bnx9-e6tj) supplies type, dates, CRFN and amount for that page in one `$where=document_id in(...)` call. Ordered newest first (document ids are date-prefixed; pre-1966 `FT_` microfilm ids sort last). Optional `doc_type` keeps only that ACRIS code (e.g. DEED) within each page; the page still advances through all the lot's documents, so a filtered page may hold fewer than `limit` documents while `next_cursor` is set. Paged with `limit` / `cursor` (row offset into Legals). A lot with no recorded documents but present in PLUTO is a successful empty page; a BBL that neither ACRIS nor PLUTO knows is `not_found`. The open-data extract lags the live City Register by weeks (Master last updated 2026-09-08 at capture); `acris_url` links each document to the authoritative page.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `documents` as the primary payload key.

200.description:
Permits issued by the Department of Buildings for one building (BIN), from NYC Open Data DOB Permit Issuance (SODA dataset ipu4-2q9a, the BIS system: every construction, plumbing, equipment and demolition permit since 1989, updated daily). Ordered newest job first (`job__ DESC, permit_sequence__ DESC`: job numbers are 9-digit and increase over time; renewals of one job follow the initial permit). Each row is shaped (job number, types, status, ISO dates, permittee and owner business names) and carried whole in `fields`. Paged with `limit` / `cursor`. An empty first page triggers a cross-check of the DOB Violations and ECB Violations datasets for the same BIN: no row anywhere is `not_found` (unknown BIN); a known building with no permits is a successful empty page. DOB NOW filings (post-2020 work filed outside BIS) are not in this dataset.

200.description:
Resolve a free-text NYC address to its Borough-Block-Lot (BBL) and Building Identification Number (BIN) with the Department of City Planning's GeoSearch API (https://geosearch.planninglabs.nyc/v2/search, a Pelias geocoder over the Property Address Directory). Returns up to `limit` candidate matches ordered by GeoSearch relevance, each with the normalized address, borough, ZIP, coordinates and the PAD `bbl` / `bin` that key every other function of this program. Zero matches is a successful empty result (`count: 0`), not an error. Anonymous, no token.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `matches` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accuracy` | string | point or centroid. |
| `bbl` | string | 10-digit Borough-Block-Lot from PAD (`addendum.pad.bbl`); the key for `property` and `acris_documents`. Null when the match carries no PAD record. |
| `bin` | string | 7-digit Building Identification Number from PAD (`addendum.pad.bin`); the key for `dob_permits` and `dob_violations`. |
| `borough` | string | Manhattan, Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens or Staten Island. |
| `confidence` | number | Pelias confidence 0-1. |
| `gid` | string | Pelias global id (`nycpad:venue:88717`). |
| `house_number` | string |  |
| `label` | string | Full label as GeoSearch renders it, e.g. `350 5 AVENUE, New York, NY, USA`. |
| `latitude` | number |  |
| `layer` | string | Pelias layer: address, venue, street, ... |
| `locality` | string |  |
| `longitude` | number |  |
| `match_type` | string | Pelias match type: exact, interpolated, fallback, ... |
| `name` | string | Normalized address line (`350 5 AVENUE`). |
| `neighbourhood` | string |  |
| `pad_version` | string | Property Address Directory release the BBL/BIN come from (`26c`). |
| `postal_code` | string |  |
| `street` | string | Street name in the city's normalized form (`5 AVENUE`). |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Search the Georgia business registry (POST /BusinessSearch) by business name, control number, registered agent name, officer (principal) name or designated agent name, with the site's Contains / StartsWith / ExactMatch criteria. Returns the results grid as displayed: business name, control number, business type, principal office address, registered or designated agent name, status, and the site's internal numeric business_id that `get_business`, `get_filing_history` and `get_name_history` take. A former name that matches the query is listed as its own row carrying the entity's business_id and control number with null business_type, address, agent and status; the current-name row with the same business_id carries them. 25 rows per page. The site's StartsWith is a normalised word match rather than a strict prefix (`Delta` also finds `Bold Delta Kappa Foundation`); Contains is the broadest. Page 1 carries the true totals; on later pages the site's pager is unreliable for a stateless request, so total_pages and total_records are null there and the continuation is derived from a full 25-row page. A search with no match is a valid empty result (the site's 'No data found.'), not an error. Broad searches (a common agent name) can take 30 s or more upstream.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent_name` | string | 'Registered / Designated Agent Name' column; null when blank or 'NONE'. |
| `business_id` | string | The site's internal numeric id (from navigateToBusinessInfo), the key for get_business, get_filing_history and get_name_history. |
| `business_name` | string |  |
| `business_type` | string | Entity class as displayed (e.g. Domestic Limited Liability Company, Foreign Profit Corporation, Name Reservation); null on a former-name row (the site lists a matched former name as its own row with the entity's business_id and control_number but no type, address, agent or status; the current-name row of the same business_id carries them). |
| `control_number` | string | Public Georgia control number as displayed (alphanumeric, e.g. H853425, 0453350, 21282188); null for rows without one (name reservations). |
| `principal_office_address` | string | One-line address as displayed; null when the cell is blank, a bare ',' (former-name rows) or the site shows 'NONE' (name reservations). |
| `status` | string | Status as displayed (e.g. Active/Compliance, Active/Noncompliance, Dissolved, Admin. Dissolved, Terminated, Withdrawn, Expired for a name reservation); free text. Null only on a former-name row (business_type null too). |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

value.text:
WARNING LETTER
WL # 724202

September 14, 2026

Dear Mr. Bonnell:

You registered your facility with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as an outsourcing facility under section 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) [21 U.S.C. § 353b]1 on December 13, 2013, and most recently on December 5, 2025. From October 20, 2025, to October 30, 2025, an FDA investigator inspected your facility, SCA Pharmaceuticals, LLC located at 8821 Knoedl Court, Little Rock, Arkansas 72205. During the inspection, the investigator noted serious deficiencies in your practices for producing drug products intended or expected to be sterile, which put patients at risk.

FDA issued a Form FDA 483 to your facility on October 30, 2025. We reviewed your November 21, 2025, and December 31, 2025, responses to our Form FDA 483 in detail and acknowledge receipt of your subsequent correspondence. Based on this inspection, it appears you produced drugs that violate the FDCA.

A. Compounded Drug Products under the FDCA

Under section 503B(b) of the FDCA, a compounder can register as an outsourcing facility with FDA. Drug products compounded by or under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist in an outsourcing facility qualify for exemptions from the drug approval requirements in section 505 of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 355(a)], the requirement in section 502(f)(1) of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 352(f)(1)] that labeling bear adequate directions for use and the Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements in section 582 of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 360eee-1] if the conditions in section 503B of the FDCA are met.

An outsourcing facility, which is defined in section 503B(d)(4) of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 353b(d)(4)], is a facility at one geographic location or address that — (i) is engaged in the compounding of sterile drugs; (ii) has elected to register as an outsourcing facility; and (iii) complies with all of the requirements of this section. Outsourcing facilities must comply with other applicable provisions of the FDCA, including section 501(a)(2)(B) [21 U.S.C. § 351(a)(2)(B)], regarding current good manufacturing practice (CGMP), and section 501(a)(2)(A) [21 U.S.C. § 351(a)(2)(A)], regarding insanitary conditions. Generally, CGMP requirements for the preparation of drug products are established in Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) parts 210 and 211.

B. Violations of the FDCA

Adulterated Drug Products

The FDA investigator collected evidence indicating that drug products intended or expected to be sterile were prepared, packed, or held under insanitary conditions, whereby they may have become contaminated with filth or rendered injurious to health, causing your drug products to be adulterated under section 501(a)(2)(A) of the FDCA. For example, the investigator collected evidence indicating that:

1. Your facility lacked routine and rigorous certification of the ISO 5 areas, including airflow visualization studies performed under dynamic conditions.

2. Your firm did not perform adequate product evaluation and take appropriate corrective action after microbial contamination was recovered within the ISO 5 aseptic processing area.

3. Your component control is not adequately designed or maintained to prevent contamination of product contact surfaces due to the presence of foreign (unusual) material between the stopper ribs of syringes.

4. Your compounding technicians and aseptic assistants employ poor practices which introduce risk of microbial contamination into the ISO 5 classified critical areas during production of drugs intended to be sterile.

For example, during the production of Fentanyl Citrate 2 mcg/mL Bupivacaine HCl 0.125% lot #1125035913 and/or Methadone HCl 10 mg/mL lot #1125035922, your compounding technicians:

a. Moved quickly in a critical area or in an area immediately adjacent to a critical area such that unidirectional airflow is likely to be disrupted.

b. Leaned into the hood, allowing their head and upper body to enter the ISO 5 classified critical area, thereby disrupting unidirectional airflow.

c. Blocked first pass air by placing gloved hands directly over the following:

i. Hanging IV bag ports when making sterile connections.

ii. The IV bag ports when disinfecting prior to filling.

iii. The open filled syringes and the syringe cap trays during the process of screwing caps onto the syringes.

d. Conducted aseptic operations on or directly above the hood deck surface in vertical flow hoods, which prevents unidirectional first air with minimal turbulence from surrounding aseptic operations during sterile connections and filling of drug products intended or expected to be sterile into open sterile containers.

e. Regularly rested their arms on the work surface of the hood during aseptic production. This practice may introduce contamination into the ISO 5 work area.

Additionally, your aseptic assistants:

a. Moved quickly in an area immediately adjacent to a critical area such that unidirectional airflow is likely to be disrupted.

b. Used disinfectant in a manner insufficient to achieve adequate levels of disinfection of materials, such as the IV bag ports, during transfer into the ISO 5 classified critical areas by spraying very quickly or from a significant distance or failing to treat both sides of the IV bags. Prior to disinfection, aseptic assistants regularly touched the IV bag ports in the ISO 7 area with their gloved hands.

5. Your environmental monitoring program lacks adequate routine environmental monitoring that captures data representative of aseptic production conditions. For example, during the production of Fentanyl Citrate 2 mcg/mL Bupivacaine HCl 0.125% lot #1125035913:

a. The active air sampler is placed to the far right of the hood instead of adjacent to the areas where aseptic operations occur, including the left and center portions of the ISO 5 classified hood.

b. Compounding technicians do not always carefully roll their individual fingers across the media touch plate during personnel monitoring. The compounding technician quickly touched each fingertip to the media plates instead of methodically rolling their fingertips.

6. Your firm failed to perform adequate airflow visualization studies under dynamic conditions to demonstrate unidirectional airflow within the ISO 5 area. Your airflow visualization studies are deficient because:

a. The studies do not clearly demonstrate that the airflow pattern sweeps over and away from the critical areas near and on the ISO 5 classified LAF hood work surface where aseptic operations occur. Instead, the smoke appears to arc out of the hood significantly higher than the critical area and then travel up toward the ceiling in the surrounding ISO 7 classified area.

b. In your most recent airflow visualization study VAL-25-044-FR, you indicated that (b)(4) people are allowed in ISO 7 (b)(4) Room (b)(4) during aseptic operations; however, the smoke study videos provided during the FDA inspection only include a maximum of (b)(4) people, and fail to demonstrate that airflow patterns inside the ISO 5 classified critical areas are not impacted by a large number of personnel moving inside cleanroom Room (b)(4).

The FDA investigator also collected evidence indicating CGMP violations at your facility, that caused your drug products to be adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FDCA. The violations include, for example:

1. Your firm failed to establish and follow appropriate written procedures that are designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile, and that include validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes (21 CFR 211.113(b)).

2. Your firm failed to establish an adequate air supply filtered through high-efficiency particulate air filters under positive pressure in the aseptic processing areas (21 CFR 211.42(c)(10)(iii)).

3. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192).

4. Your firm failed to establish laboratory controls that include scientifically sound and appropriate specifications, standards, sampling plans, and test procedures designed to assure that components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, labeling, and drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b)).

5. Your firm failed to establish adequate written responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit and to follow written procedures applicable to the quality control unit (21 CFR 211.22(d)). Specifically, our review of the data collected during the inspection revealed that your firm does not maintain the production video recordings which are used to determine root causes and corrective actions during investigations. For example, after recovering microbial contamination inside the ISO 5 classified critical area during the production of Ketamine HCl 10 mg/mL lot 1125035065, your Quality Unit evaluated the production video recording as part of excursion investigation EXC-2025-0045 to examine aseptic practices for potential root causes. However, instead of retaining the video recording as a quality related document, you only retained still images. Your Chief Quality Officer stated that video recordings are kept for approximately (b)(4) before being overwritten.

Outsourcing facilities must comply with CGMP requirements under section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FDCA. FDA’s regulations regarding CGMP requirements for the preparation of drug products have been established in 21 CFR parts 210 and 211. FDA intends to promulgate more specific CGMP regulations for outsourcing facilities. FDA has issued a revised draft guidance, Current Good Manufacturing Practice — Guidance for Human Drug Compounding Outsourcing Facilities under Section 503B of the FD&C Act. This draft guidance, when finalized, will describe FDA’s expectations regarding outsourcing facilities and the CGMP requirements in 21 CFR parts 210 and 211 until more specific CGMP regulations for outsourcing facilities are promulgated.

Under section 301(a) of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 331(a)], the introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce of any drug that is adulterated is a prohibited act. Further, it is also a prohibited act under section 301(k) of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 331(k)] to do any act with respect to a drug, if such act is done while the drug is held for sale after shipment in interstate commerce and results in the drug being adulterated.

C. Corrective Actions

We have reviewed your facility’s responses to the Form FDA 483 dated November 21, 2025, and December 31, 2025.

Some of your corrective actions appear adequate. However, we are unable to fully evaluate some of your corrective actions due to lack of adequate supporting documentation:

1. Although you stated that you performed airflow visualization studies in all (b)(4) hoods, you did not clearly demonstrate that these studies were performed in all (b)(4) hoods during the most recent airflow visualization assessment, performed in 2025. Additionally, while you concluded that the hoods are identical and therefore functionally equivalent, this approach does not account for potential variations in the HEPA filter performance, for example, resulting from particulate accumulation over time, nor the impact of physical placement of hoods within the room—including proximity to doors, return vents, and other environmental factors that may affect airflow where production activities are occurring.

Some of your corrective actions appear deficient:

1. You did not demonstrate that the probable root cause of inadequate material sanitization had no impact on the released portions of the batch associated with microbial excursions in the ISO 5 classified areas during production. You indicated both in your investigations and in your response that your material sanitization process is robust, but also concluded that the microbial contamination was most likely due to inadequate material sanitization.

You failed to demonstrate that microbial contamination was not present in the materials associated with the released portions of the batch. You did not demonstrate that the material sanitization process for the released portions of the batches did not include the same deficiencies as the material sanitization for the rejected portion of the batch. Further, you failed to initiate any corrective and preventative action plans to determine whether you need to improve your material sanitization process to prevent reoccurrence.

2. It appears that your visual inspection system is inadequate because you classify particulate defects as major and therefore only characterize and investigate the observed particles when the defect rate is above the major defect threshold of (b)(4)%. Extrinsic particulates should be classified as critical, and the intrinsic particulates should be evaluated based on multiple factors, including particle size and route of administration, to determine the appropriate defect classification. Your SOP ILP-001-LR, Product Inspection and Defect Classification, states, “If a DRL (Defect Rate Limit) threshold is exceeded related to ‘Particulate/material in solution,’ the particulate/material must be identified during the event.” According to your visual inspection data, you detected between (b)(4) and (b)(4) particles in (b)(4) separate lots between April 2025 and September 2025, only (b)(4) lots of which exceeded the (b)(4)% threshold for major defects. According to your Deviation log, only (b)(4) defect incidents were investigated between April 2025 and September 2025, and these were related to any Defect Rate Limit Threshold Exceedance, not just those involving particles. Therefore, you do not have an adequate system in place to ensure that you identify and appropriately investigate contaminating particles.

3. You did not commit to revising the minor defect classification for “[f]oreign (unusual) material, e.g., cardboard trapped between stopper ribs” to account for the criticality of the foreign material. While you noted that any units exhibiting this defect are rejected, the defect rate limit applied to minor defects ((b)(4)%) is not appropriate for adequately investigating, trending, and performing corrective actions, as necessary, to mitigate this contamination risk.

You did not provide adequate documentation to demonstrate that foreign materials are contained within the ribs of the syringe stoppers in non-product-contact area and will not pose contamination risks to the drug product. In addition, the syringe filling process demonstrates that the foreign material does come into contact with product-contact area of the syringes. For example, any cardboard particles trapped within the syringe ribs may be pressed against the inner syringe wall during filling, potentially introducing particles onto a surface that subsequently contacts the drug product solution.

In addition to the issues discussed above, you should note that CGMP requires the implementation of quality oversight and controls over the manufacture of drugs, including the safety of raw materials, materials used in drug manufacturing, and finished drug products. See section 501 of the FDCA. If you choose to contract with a laboratory to perform some functions required by CGMP, it is essential that you select a qualified contractor and that you maintain sufficient oversight of the contractor’s operations to ensure that it is fully CGMP compliant. Regardless of whether you rely on a contract facility, you are responsible for assuring that drugs you produce are neither adulterated nor misbranded. [See 21 CFR 210.1(b), 21 CFR 200.10(b).]

FDA strongly recommends that your management undertake a comprehensive assessment of operations, including facility design, procedures, personnel, processes, maintenance, materials, and systems. In particular, this review should assess your aseptic processing operations. A third-party consultant with relevant sterile drug manufacturing expertise should assist you in conducting this comprehensive evaluation.

D. Conclusion

The violations cited in this letter are not intended to be an all-inclusive statement of violations at your facility. You are responsible for investigating and determining the causes of any violations and for preventing their recurrence or the occurrence of other violations. It is your responsibility to ensure that your firm complies with all requirements of federal law, including FDA regulations.

You should take prompt action to address any violations. Failure to adequately address any violations may result in legal action without further notice, including, without limitation, seizure and injunction.

Within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of this letter, please notify this office in writing of the specific steps that you have taken to address any violations. Please include an explanation of each step being taken to prevent the recurrence of violations, as well as copies of related documentation. This letter notifies you of our concerns and provides you an opportunity to address them. If you believe your products are not in violation of the FDCA, include your reasoning and any supporting information for our consideration. If you cannot completely address this matter within fifteen (15) working days, state the reason for the delay and the time within which you will do so.

All correspondence should refer to the Warning Letter Number above (# 724202) and include a subject line that clearly identifies the submission as a Response to Warning Letter. If you have questions regarding the contents of this letter, please contact compoundinginspections@fda.hhs.gov.

Sincerely,
/S/

Matthew J. Lash
Acting Director
Office of Compounding Quality and Compliance
Office of Compliance
Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

cc: Scott P. Luce, Chief Executive Officer

____________________

1 See Pub. L. No. 113-54, § 102(a), 127 Stat. 587, 587-588 (2013).

200.description:
One human gene's approved HGNC record, from whatever you have: a symbol, alias or previous symbol, an HGNC, NCBI Gene, Ensembl, UniProt, RefSeq, MGI or RGD ID, or a genenames.org URL. Says how the input matched, and returns the approved symbol and name, aliases, previous symbols, locus type, location, gene groups and cross-references (NCBI Gene, Ensembl, UniProt, OMIM, RefSeq, MANE Select, CCDS, MGI, RGD, Orphanet, PubMed). An alias shared by several genes is an `ambiguous` result listing every candidate, and a withdrawn HGNC ID that was merged resolves to the gene it went into. Unknown genes are `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candidates` | object[] | Other records the input matches (for `ambiguous`, all of them), strongest match first. |
| `gene` | object | The resolved record; null when `resolution` is `ambiguous`. |
| `input` | string | The gene string as given. |
| `license` | object | HGNC releases all data under CC0 (genenames.org/about/license); attribution is recommended, not required. |
| `matched_on` | string | How the input matched `gene`, or what the ambiguous candidates share. |
| `note` | string | One plain sentence on the resolution, e.g. `p53 is an alias of TP53 (HGNC:11998); the approved symbol is TP53.` |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `resolution` | string | `resolved` (one approved record), `ambiguous` (several records tie, so `gene` is null and `candidates` lists them) or `withdrawn` (only a withdrawn entry matches). |

200.description:
Search HGNC's human genes by free text, where every word must match a symbol, alias, name or other field (`kinase`, `17p13.1`, `zinc finger`), or by HGNC field syntax (`symbol:ZNF*`, `name:"potassium channel" AND locus_type:"gene with protein product"`). Filters for locus group and status; approved genes only by default. An exact symbol, previous-symbol or alias match ranks first. Each result has the HGNC ID, approved symbol and name, locus group and type, location, aliases, previous symbols, and NCBI Gene, Ensembl and UniProt IDs. Offset-paginated; an empty result is a valid empty page.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alias_symbols` | string[] | Other symbols in use for this gene (not approved). |
| `ensembl_gene_id` | string | Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...). |
| `hgnc_id` | string | HGNC ID, e.g. `HGNC:11998`. |
| `location` | string | Cytogenetic location, e.g. `17p13.1`; null when HGNC records none. |
| `locus_group` | string | Locus group, e.g. `protein-coding gene`, `non-coding RNA`, `pseudogene`, `other`. |
| `locus_type` | string | Locus type, e.g. `gene with protein product`, `RNA, long non-coding`. |
| `name` | string | Approved gene name. |
| `ncbi_gene_id` | string | NCBI Gene (Entrez) ID; joins gene-ncbi-nlm-nih-gov. |
| `previous_symbols` | string[] | Symbols this gene was approved under before. |
| `score` | number | HGNC relevance score. |
| `source_url` | string | The gene's symbol report on genenames.org. |
| `status` | string | `approved`, or `withdrawn` for an entry HGNC no longer maintains. |
| `symbol` | string | Approved symbol (for a withdrawn entry, the symbol it had). |
| `uniprot_ids` | string[] | UniProtKB accessions; join uniprot-org. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

value.description_html:
Located just minutes from downtown Orlando, Dubsdread features the oldest public layout in the area, originally designed in 1923 and renovated in 2008. This classic course has plenty of history attached to it as the former site of the Orlando Open, when it hosted such golf legends as Sam Snead, Ben Hogan and Claude Harmon.

Today, golfers are treated to the same beautiful scenery and challenges of the original course, including narrow fairways and heavily bunkered, "postage stamp" style greens. A full restaurant and banquet facility complete the ultimate golfing experience.
value.information:
**ATTENTION GOLFERS**
The driving range is closed until further notice.

GREAT SPECIAL AVAILABLE TO NON-RESIDENTS AS WELL AS RESIDENTS OF FL!

TAX NOT INCLUDED.

Please bring a copy of your reservation to the golf course. We ask that our customers adhere to golf course dress code: No denim allowed, collared shirt is required, soft spikes only. Players & guests are required to follow all course policies and procedures as outlined by the staff.
value.name: Dubsdread Golf Course

review_summaries.summary: Dubsdread's greens consistently rank among Orlando's best, rolling quick and true even under heavy traffic and wet conditions. Exceptionally friendly staff and fair pricing make this uniquely-laid-out course a standout value in Central Florida.

value.terms_and_conditions:
Terms and Conditions

At Legacy, we thrive to bring you the best products at the price you choose. We are an online auction featuring various categories of items. We are not a retail store that sell only new items, so make sure to check the descriptions and images, before bidding. Some are sealed and some are open boxes, mainly customer returns from popular online retailers, overstock shelf pulls and unclaimed packages! Our best efforts are made to represent all items accurately in descriptions and photographs; however, all items are ultimately sold on an 'as is, where is' basis, with all faults.


Product Description
Brand new: refers to a product or item that does not show signs of use, contained in their original packaging, but external package sealing might be open for inspection and identification purposes.


New open box: refers to a product or item that does not show signs of use, contained in their original packaging, and there are some signs of altering the internal packaging. The item is in new condition and might previously tested by anyone.


Lightly Used: refers to a product or item that has been previously owned or used but is in excellent condition, with little to no signs of wear or use. It may have been used briefly or infrequently and has been well-maintained.


Used: refers to a product or item that has been previously owned or used by someone else. It may show signs of wear or use.


"As-is": refers to a product or item that is being sold in its current condition, without any warranties or guarantees from the seller regarding its quality and maybe used or damaged or missing parts.


Registration
A valid Ontario credit card is required to register. It is important to provide accurate information in relation to your credit card. The address on file must match the billing address on your file for payment to go through. First name and last name required when registering. Your credit card will not be charged unless you win. You can verify winning bids by logging into your account after the auction closes and checking each lot. If the lot says "Status", you have won. If it says "Outbid" you have not won.


Final Bids
All our bids are final and cannot be reversed. Please do your due diligence in making sure that you do want the product before placing a bid. We have the right to add or remove any items on the current running auction. This is usually done to ensure product information accuracy and to avoid any possible mistakes. We usually describe all, and any information related to the product in our description, and sometimes we provide actual pictures of our products unless it is sealed. Please scroll through all photos and read descriptions. Our best efforts are made to represent all items accurately in descriptions and photographs; however, all items are ultimately sold on an 'as is, where is' basis, with all faults.


Soft close
Items close at regular intervals. To prevent a bidder from 'sniping', all bids made in the last minute of the auction will force an item to stay open for an additional 2 minutes. This will continue until all bidding has ceased.


Invoices and clerking
Invoices will be created within 24 hours after the auction close. Our invoices will include item quantity and description, detailed breakdown of payment (Total extended price, Buyer Premium, Handling, Tax, and Invoice total). All our invoices will include a 18% buyer premium auction fee, a $1 CAD per item handling fee, and 13% sales tax. If an item is in any part tax exempt, bidders may keep their invoice and claim the exemption on their income tax.


Payment
Payment is due within 24 hours after auction close. If the card on file is declined, it will be your responsibility to remit payment and clear the outstanding balance, otherwise your items have a high potential of being considered abandoned, and a very high risk of getting blocked from bidding again.

Balances over $300, will need to provide payment information by phone, or email after the end of the auction, in order to complete the sale. 


Shipping and Handling
All purchases shipped over $300 will require special conditions, including proof of signature upon delivery, and therefore all administrative shipping fees will apply.

auction.terms_and_conditions:
Terms and Conditions

At Legacy, we thrive to bring you the best products at the price you choose. We are an online auction featuring various categories of items. We are not a retail store that sell only new items, so make sure to check the descriptions and images, before bidding. Some are sealed and some are open boxes, mainly customer returns from popular online retailers, overstock shelf pulls and unclaimed packages! Our best efforts are made to represent all items accurately in descriptions and photographs; however, all items are ultimately sold on an 'as is, where is' basis, with all faults.


Product Description
Brand new: refers to a product or item that does not show signs of use, contained in their original packaging, but external package sealing might be open for inspection and identification purposes.


New open box: refers to a product or item that does not show signs of use, contained in their original packaging, and there are some signs of altering the internal packaging. The item is in new condition and might previously tested by anyone.


Lightly Used: refers to a product or item that has been previously owned or used but is in excellent condition, with little to no signs of wear or use. It may have been used briefly or infrequently and has been well-maintained.


Used: refers to a product or item that has been previously owned or used by someone else. It may show signs of wear or use.


"As-is": refers to a product or item that is being sold in its current condition, without any warranties or guarantees from the seller regarding its quality and maybe used or damaged or missing parts.


Registration
A valid Ontario credit card is required to register. It is important to provide accurate information in relation to your credit card. The address on file must match the billing address on your file for payment to go through. First name and last name required when registering. Your credit card will not be charged unless you win. You can verify winning bids by logging into your account after the auction closes and checking each lot. If the lot says "Status", you have won. If it says "Outbid" you have not won.


Final Bids
All our bids are final and cannot be reversed. Please do your due diligence in making sure that you do want the product before placing a bid. We have the right to add or remove any items on the current running auction. This is usually done to ensure product information accuracy and to avoid any possible mistakes. We usually describe all, and any information related to the product in our description, and sometimes we provide actual pictures of our products unless it is sealed. Please scroll through all photos and read descriptions. Our best efforts are made to represent all items accurately in descriptions and photographs; however, all items are ultimately sold on an 'as is, where is' basis, with all faults.


Soft close
Items close at regular intervals. To prevent a bidder from 'sniping', all bids made in the last minute of the auction will force an item to stay open for an additional 2 minutes. This will continue until all bidding has ceased.


Invoices and clerking
Invoices will be created within 24 hours after the auction close. Our invoices will include item quantity and description, detailed breakdown of payment (Total extended price, Buyer Premium, Handling, Tax, and Invoice total). All our invoices will include a 18% buyer premium auction fee, a $1 CAD per item handling fee, and 13% sales tax. If an item is in any part tax exempt, bidders may keep their invoice and claim the exemption on their income tax.


Payment
Payment is due within 24 hours after auction close. If the card on file is declined, it will be your responsibility to remit payment and clear the outstanding balance, otherwise your items have a high potential of being considered abandoned, and a very high risk of getting blocked from bidding again.

Balances over $300, will need to provide payment information by phone, or email after the end of the auction, in order to complete the sale. 


Shipping and Handling
All purchases shipped over $300 will require special conditions, including proof of signature upon delivery, and therefore all administrative shipping fees will apply.

post.description: Start here to find lot ids (for `lot` and `lot_bids`) and auction ids, or to list one auction's catalog (auction_id, sort LOT_NUMBER). For sold prices of a past auction pass archived=true with its auction_id.

archived.description: Search HiBid's archive of completed auctions (results carry price_realized). Requires auction_id: the archive is only served per auction.

auction_id.description: Restrict to one auction (HiBid eventId, from `search_auctions` or a /catalog/{id} URL). Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

category_id.description: HiBid category id, e.g. 700001 (Antiques & Collectibles) or 40125 (Coins - US - Dollars); `lot` returns a lot's category path with ids. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

country.description:
Country name as HiBid spells it.

Provider reference: allowed values ["United States", "Canada"].

miles.description:
Radius around zip in miles. Requires zip.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 5000.

page.description:
1-based page; `next_page` of the previous result.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000; default 1.

page_size.description:
page_size

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 25.

query.description: Keyword search over lot titles and descriptions.

sort.description:
NO_ORDER is HiBid's default relevance order; LOT_NUMBER for catalog order within an auction; TIME_LEFT for lots closing soonest.

Provider reference: allowed values ["NO_ORDER", "LOT_NUMBER", "TIME_LEFT"]; default "NO_ORDER".

state.description: Two-letter US state or Canadian province code of the auction location, e.g. FL, ON. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

status.description:
OPEN: lots accepting bids now (default). ALL: open, upcoming and closed lots of current auctions. TOP: HiBid's featured 'top lots' ranking.

Provider reference: allowed values ["OPEN", "ALL", "TOP"]; default "OPEN".

zip.description: Postal code for a radius search; combine with miles (default 50). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9 -]{3,10}$.
