releases.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.22.4

**Release Date:** October 21, 2026

Patch release. Desktop stops showing suggestion pills above the composer, plus small plugin and dashboard fixes, for the CLI and installer, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud.

## Fixes

- **Desktop no longer shows suggestion pills above the composer.** The pills appeared for no clear reason, mostly nudging you to set up MCP servers. They and the helpers that only they used are gone. (#142559)

- **Plugins that install nothing skip the dependency consent step.** A plugin that declares no dependencies, or whose `pyproject.toml` installs nothing, now enables without an empty consent prompt. (#142569)

- **Dashboard: WhatsApp can be safely re-paired after logging out.** (#142439)

- **Desktop plugin review:** the surface lint no longer flags prototype writes; reviewers check them by hand. (#142586)

- **Desktop: the approval-mode chip follows the active profile's mode.** (#142565)

- **Release builds:** the desktop bundle's pre-build check gets enough time to verify archived build inputs when storage is slow. (#142623)

Also new in the plugin catalog: bubblewrap (bwrap terminal backend on Linux), Singularity/Apptainer, mcp-serve (Hermes as an MCP server), agent-importers (`hermes import-agent`, now with Cursor), inbox and workflow-record from Hermes Labs. Telegram Business moves to the Hermes Labs community tier.

## About this release

Measured at commit `4d04303818b`, the window since v0.22.3 contains **14 non-merge commits** across **82 changed files** (+1,475 / −3,022) and **13 merged PRs**.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.

- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.

- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.

- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: v0.22.3...v0.22.4

# Hermes Agent v0.22.3

**Release Date:** October 21, 2026

Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~620 PRs merged since v0.22.2 into a stable release for the CLI and installer, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.23.0.

## About this release

Measured at commit `5b147ab036d`, the window since v0.22.2 contains **2,911 non-merge commits** across **4,206 changed files** (+360,278 / −64,308), about **620 merged PRs** and **326 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: MCP progress notifications streamed as live tool progress, a refreshed classic CLI layout (glyph transcript, status line under the composer, two-line header), OAuth clients that plugins declare and Hermes signs in and refreshes, `hermes plugins update` offering every available plugin update plus an Update button for git-installed plugins in Desktop, steering and editing a queued prompt from Desktop, a guided subagent model and provider picker in Desktop, a live `/loop` countdown row in the CLI and TUI, opt-in Telegram DM topic transfer, a `post_compaction` plugin hook, a capabilities catalog, the Microsoft Store build going live automatically when a release publishes, session auto-prune back to opt-in with a one-time prompt when disk runs low, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and one-slot DFlash drafts in the local runtime, and dozens of new plugin catalog entries.

**Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.23.0**, which will document everything from v0.22.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.

- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.

- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.

- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

value.content:
## How It Works

Two files make up the agent's memory:

| File | Purpose | Char Limit |
|------|---------|------------|
| **MEMORY.md** | Agent's personal notes — environment facts, conventions, things learned | 2,200 chars (~800 tokens) |
| **USER.md** | User profile — your preferences, communication style, expectations | 1,375 chars (~500 tokens) |

Both are stored in `~/.hermes/memories/` and are injected into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start. The agent manages its own memory via the `memory` tool — it can add, patch, or remove entries.

:::caution One agent per Hermes home
Don't point two agent processes at the same Hermes home directory. Memory writes are automatic and load back into the system prompt at session start, so two writers sharing one home will compound each other's entries into state neither of them (nor you) authored. Memory is scoped per [profile](../profiles.md) by design — give a second agent its own profile, and if they need shared memory, use an [external memory provider](./memory-providers.md) instead.
:::

:::info
Character limits keep memory focused. Memory does **not** auto-compact: when a
write would exceed the limit, the `memory` tool returns an error instead of
silently dropping entries. The agent then makes room itself — consolidating or
removing entries in the same turn before retrying (see [What Happens When Memory
is Full](#what-happens-when-memory-is-full)). Note that `patch` is also bound
by the limit: a patch that lengthens an entry can still overflow, so the new
text must be shortened (or another entry removed) to fit.
:::
value.description: How Hermes Agent remembers across sessions — MEMORY.md, USER.md, and session search

value.desktop_packages:
Download the package for your platform from the
[Hermes website](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/).

- **Windows:** open the `.appinstaller` download with Windows App Installer.
  It installs the signed MSIX bundle and records its update source.
  Microsoft Store packages have separate Store ownership.
- **macOS:** open the DMG, then copy `Hermes.app` to Applications. The ZIP
  artifact carries the signed app used by the automatic updater.

Bundled packages contain the agent, Python, supported dependencies, and prebuilt
interfaces. First launch does not build that base runtime. Provider access and
optional integrations can still require network access.

A `Hermes-Setup` bootstrap installer is different: it downloads a source
installation and builds the desktop app. See [Hermes Desktop](../user-guide/desktop.md).

There is no separate remote-only Desktop download. To use Desktop with a Hermes
backend on another machine, install one of the packages above and connect it
from **Settings → Gateways**; see
[Connecting to a remote backend](../user-guide/desktop.md#connecting-to-a-remote-backend).

:::note
The macOS installer is **Apple Silicon only**. macOS on x86 (Intel) processors is [not a supported platform](./platform-support.md#unsupported).
:::

value.summary: The self-improving AI agent built by Nous Research. # Jev Documentation: Using the TypeSafe Decision Model on OpenRouter

> The OpenRouter hub for Jev, the TypeSafe decision model. What Jev is, how to get access, the Decisions API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, cookbooks, pricing, and demos

## Jev on OpenRouter

Jev is a structured decision model from [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai), and the first of its System One models. Send it application state and one or more typed questions, and get back a typed answer with probabilities instead of generated text. `typesafe/jev-1.13` (or the `~typesafe/jev-latest` alias) is available to anyone with an [OpenRouter API key](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys), and billed to your OpenRouter account.

This is the index for every Jev resource on OpenRouter, and your entry point to the upstream TypeSafe documentation.

### What Jev is

Jev is a [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one) model. System One models make fast, structured decisions for software. They are suited for any routing, classification, verification, ranking, or other decision point in your app where a predictable typed answer matters more than generated prose.

Jev answers three kinds of question, called primitives:

| Primitive                                            | Question it answers                       | What comes back                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice) | Which one of these options?               | The selected option, a probability for each option, and a confidence value            |
| [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul)     | Does this condition hold?                 | The probability of yes                                                                |
| [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score)   | Where does this fall on an ordered scale? | A probability-weighted position, a probability for each level, and a confidence value |

Because the output is typed, code branches on it directly. Jev does not produce reasoning traces, explanations, or free-form text. It is not a drop-in replacement for a chat model. It replaces the prompt-and-parse step where you were asking an LLM a narrow question and extracting a label from its answer.

Below are the key facts, current as of the [Jev model page](https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-1.13):

* **Model ID:** `typesafe/jev-1.13`. The `~typesafe/jev-latest` alias tracks the newest release.
* **Input:** text, as a `state` object plus your `questions`. Context length is 32,000 tokens.
* **Output:** typed decisions. Output tokens are free. You pay per input token at the price on the model page.
* **Provider:** TypeSafe, routed through OpenRouter.

### Get access to Jev

There's no waitlist or separate TypeSafe account. Just create an [OpenRouter API key](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys), and then follow the [Jev tutorial](/docs/guides/community/jev-tutorial). Your first call takes under five minutes.

### Two ways to call Jev

Jev is exposed via two OpenRouter API surfaces, the Decisions API and the System One API. Both surfaces require the same OpenRouter API key and are billed to the same OpenRouter account.

| Surface        | Endpoint                                         | Use it when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Decisions API  | `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions` | You are calling Jev from any language with plain HTTP, or through the OpenRouter [TypeScript](/docs/client-sdks/typescript/sdks/decisions/README), [Python](/docs/client-sdks/python/sdks/decisions/README), or [Go](/docs/client-sdks/go/sdks/decisions/README) SDK |
| System One API | `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone`    | You already use the TypeSafe JavaScript or Python SDK and want to switch it to OpenRouter by changing the base URL                                                                                                                                    |

The [Jev SDK guide](/docs/guides/community/typesafe-sdk) documents the System One path. The [Decisions API reference](/docs/api/api-reference/alphadecisions/submit-a-decisions-questions-and-answers-request) covers the Decisions path.

### Cookbooks

Step-by-step recipes with runnable code:

* [Gate Agent Tool Calls with Jev](/docs/cookbook/building-agents/gate-tool-calls-with-jev) checks each risky agent tool call against the user's request so safe calls run, unsupported calls are refused, and only ambiguous calls pause for a human.
* [Cut LLM Cost with a Jev-Verified Cascade](/docs/cookbook/evaluate-and-optimize/jev-verified-cascade) drafts with a cheap model, verifies the draft against retrieved context with Jev, and escalates to a stronger model only when the check fails.

### Interactive demos

[Jev Lab](https://openrouter.ai/labs/jev) runs Jev live in the browser across several patterns, including [ticket triage](https://openrouter.ai/labs/jev/triage), [agent oversight](https://openrouter.ai/labs/jev/overseer), and [structured extraction](https://openrouter.ai/labs/jev/extract). Each demo shows you the state, the questions, and the raw probabilities Jev returns.

### TypeSafe documentation

TypeSafe maintains the concept, prompting, and SDK documentation for Jev. These are the pages to read when designing questions and thresholds:

* [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one) explains the model family and how it differs from generative models.
* [How to build with System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one) covers decomposing a workflow into judgments.
* [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state) covers what to send as context and how to reference nested fields.
* [Primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives) covers Choice, Noul, and Score in detail.
* [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence) covers reading probabilities and choosing thresholds.
* [JavaScript SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript) and [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python) are the official client references.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is Jev an LLM?**
No. Jev is a System One decision model. It returns typed answers, with probabilities associated with them. Jev doesn't return text, reasoning, or explanations. When you need prose, use a chat model. When you need a decision that your code can act on, use Jev.

**Who makes Jev?**
TypeSafe. OpenRouter routes your request to TypeSafe, then bills it to your OpenRouter account.

**How much does Jev cost?**
Jev charges for input tokens, and output tokens are free. To find the current input token price, see the [Jev model page](https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-1.13). Every Jev response includes a `usage.cost` field that tells you the cost of the response in USD.

**What is Jev's context window?**
32,000 tokens. That's the `state` you send plus the questions.

**Do I need a TypeSafe account or API key?**
No, an OpenRouter API key authenticates both the Decisions API and the TypeSafe SDK pointed at OpenRouter.

**Can Jev explain its answers?**
No, Jev doesn't return the reasoning it goes through to make its decision. It returns probabilities. If you need a written justification for the decision, you can use Jev to make the decision, then use a chat model to explain it, or if the confidence is low, you can route that case to a human.

**Where are the Jev docs?**
It's all here on OpenRouter. Once you're in, use the [TypeSafe documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai) to dig deeper into the concepts and for the SDK reference.

abstracts.text: A rotor (100) and a motor. The rotor (100) comprises: a rotor core (1) and a plurality of permanent magnets (2), wherein the rotor core (1) is provided with a plurality of mounting grooves, the plurality of permanent magnets (2) are arranged in the plurality of mounting grooves in a one-to-one correspondence manner, materials of the permanent magnets (2) in the at least two mounting grooves are different, the plurality of mounting grooves comprise a first mounting groove (11), and a permanent magnet (2) arranged in the first mounting groove (11) comprises a first magnet (21) and a second magnet (22) which are arranged in a segmented manner.

La présente invention concerne un rotor (100) et un moteur. Le rotor (100) comprend : un noyau de rotor (1) et une pluralité d'aimants permanents (2), le noyau de rotor (1) comportant une pluralité de rainures de montage, la pluralité d'aimants permanents (2) étant agencés dans la pluralité de rainures de montage à la manière d'une correspondance biunivoque, les matériaux des aimants permanents (2) dans les au moins deux rainures de montage étant différents, la pluralité de rainures de montage comprenant une première rainure de montage (11), et un aimant permanent (2) agencé dans la première rainure de montage (11) comprenant un premier aimant (21) et un second aimant (22) qui sont agencés d'une manière segmentée.
一种转子(100)和电机，转子(100)包括：转子铁芯(1)和多个永磁体(2)，转子铁芯(1)上设有多个安装槽；多个永磁体(2)一一对应地设置在多个安装槽内，至少两个安装槽内的永磁体(2)的材料不同；其中，多个安装槽包括第一安装槽(11)，设于第一安装槽(11)内的永磁体(2)包括分段设置的第一磁体(21)和第二磁体(22)。

results.abstract: [Problem] To provide a photovoltaic installation and a cleaning method therefor, with which it is possible to economically and efficiently clean light-receiving surfaces such as mirrors and solar panels used in a photovoltaic installation. [Solution] A photovoltaic installation in which a plurality of solar panels (1) are arranged with a predetermined space therebetween, said installation comprising a movement means (2) for allowing an automated light-receiving-surface cleaning robot (3) to travel and move from one solar panel (1) to a solar panel (1) adjacent thereto. After finishing cleaning the light-receiving surface of the one solar panel (1), the automated light-receiving-surface cleaning robot (3) travels and moves, via the movement means (2), to a solar panel (1) adjacent to the one solar panel (1), and cleans the light-receiving surface thereof.
results.title: PHOTOVOLTAIC INSTALLATION AND PHOTOVOLTAIC INSTALLATION CLEANING METHOD

results.abstract: A control system of a solar panel cleaning robot, for use in the solar panel cleaning robot. The control system comprises a data collection unit used for collecting at least one working parameter during proceeding of the cleaning robot; a processor connected to the data collection unit and used for sending a proceeding control instruction or a cleaning control instruction; and a storage unit connected to the processor and used for storing the working parameter of the cleaning robot during proceeding. The robot control system ensures that the robot can walk through all space of a panel without any repetition and would not fall from the edge of the panel. Therefore, the cleaning effect and the working efficiency are guaranteed.
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: CONTROL SYSTEM OF SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT

results.abstract: A solar panel cleaning robot, comprising a vehicle body (1) which is capable of driving on at least one solar panel (200); a cleaning device (2), a driving force system (3), a control system (4) and an electric power system (5) are provided inside or outside the vehicle body (1); the cleaning device (2) is configured to clean the solar panel; the driving force system (3) is configured to adjust the traveling direction and driving speed of the vehicle body (1) on the solar panel (200); the control system (4) is connected to the driving force system (3) and the cleaning device (2), respectively; the electric power system (5) is connected to the driving force system (3), the cleaning device (2) and the control system (4), respectively, and is configured to provide power for the driving force system (3), the cleaning device (2) and the control system (4). The solar panel cleaning robot can freely operate on the solar panel, efficiently removing dust and other matter stuck to the panel.
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT

results.abstract: The present invention provides a wireless charging system and wireless charging method for a solar panel cleaning robot. The wireless charging system comprises at least one solar panel, a cleaning robot, a rechargeable battery, at least one wireless power transmitting device, and a wireless power receiving device.
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: WIRELESS CHARGING SYSTEM AND WIRELESS CHARGING METHOD FOR SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT

results.abstract: Provided are a positioning device for a solar panel cleaning robot (100) and a positioning method thereof. The positioning device is used to obtain a real-time position of a vehicle body (10) on a solar panel (200). The positioning device comprises an image acquisition unit (11), a border recognition unit (12), a latitude and longitude recognition unit (13), a vehicle body position calculation unit (14), an image acquisition unit position calculation unit (15), a vehicle body center point position calculation unit (16), a GPS unit (17), a panel determination unit (18), a wireless communication unit (19) and a memory (20).
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT POSITIONING DEVICE AND POSITIONING METHOD THEREOF

results.abstract: A navigation system for a solar panel cleaning robot (100) and a navigation method thereof. The navigation system comprises an optimized route planning unit (21), a positioning device (22) and a control system (23). The optimized route planning unit (21) is arranged inside of an external server (30), and is used for calculating and planning an optimized route of the cleaning robot (100); the positioning device (22) is arranged on a vehicle body (10) of the cleaning robot (100), and is used for obtaining the real-time position of the vehicle body (10); and the control system (23) is connected to the optimized path planning unit (21) and the positioning device (22) respectively, and is used for issuing at least one control instruction according to the optimized path and the real-time position of the vehicle body (10).
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: NAVIGATION SYSTEM FOR SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT AND NAVIGATION METHOD THEREOF

results.abstract: The present invention relates to a system (100) for cleaning a photovoltaic panel. The system (100) includes a movable docking assembly (104), a base support structure (106), a lifting mechanism (102), a robot holding support (132) and a control system (138). The lifting mechanism (102) is attached to the base support structure (106). A robot is placed on a robot holding support plate (134) of the robot holding support (132). The movable docking assembly (104) is moved to the photovoltaic panel row. The robot is lifted up to the height of the photovoltaic panel and the robot moves to the photovoltaic panel row and cleans the photovoltaic panel row. After cleaning the robot returns to the movable docking assembly (104) and the movable docking assembly (104) further moves to another the photovoltaic panel row. The present invention works manually and automatically. The present invention is time saving process as invention reduces the total cleaning time of a large solar power plant.
results.title: A MOVEABLE DOCKING SYSTEM FOR PV SOLAR POWER PLANT

results.abstract: A straight-on determination apparatus for a solar panel cleaning robot, and a determination method thereof. The determination apparatus comprises an image acquisition unit (12) and an image recognition and processing unit. The image acquisition unit is arranged on a car body (10) of a solar panel cleaning robot and is used for acquiring surface image information about the solar panel on a walking line of the car body. The image recognition and processing unit is used for processing image information, and in turn judging whether the car body is walking in a straight line in a planned route on the solar panel.
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: STRAIGHT-ON DETERMINATION APPARATUS FOR SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT, AND DETERMINATION METHOD THEREOF

results.abstract: An edge positioning apparatus for a solar panel cleaning robot, and a positioning method thereof. The solar panel cleaning robot comprises a car body (10) and an edge positioning apparatus, and the car body travels or is resident on at least one solar panel (200). The edge positioning apparatus comprises an image acquisition unit (13) and an image recognition and processing unit. The image acquisition unit is arranged on the car body and is used for acquiring surface image information about the solar panel on a walking line of the car body. The image recognition and processing unit is used for processing image information, and in turn judging whether the car body is walking at an edge area of the solar panel.
results.applicant: SUZHOU RADIANT PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
results.title: EDGE POSITIONING APPARATUS FOR SOLAR PANEL CLEANING ROBOT, AND POSITIONING METHOD THEREOF

results.abstract: Autonomous robotic cleaner (ARC) for cleaning solar panels having an anchoring mechanism including at least one rechargeable power source, at least one cleaning mechanism, a controller and an anchoring mechanism, the cleaning mechanism for cleaning dirt off of a surface of the solar panels, the controller for controlling a cleaning process of the ARC and the anchoring mechanism for magnetically anchoring the ARC to an anchoring surface coupled with a solar panel, the anchoring mechanism including an arm and a drive mechanism, the arm including at least one ferromagnetic end piece and the drive mechanism being coupled with the arm, wherein the drive mechanism moves the arm between a magnetically engaged position with the anchoring surface and a magnetically disengaged position with the anchoring surface.
results.title: MAGNETIC PARKING FOR ROBOTIC CLEANER ON A SOLAR PANEL

value.project_description:
Action 6 of the Climate Resilience Planning and Development (CRPD) Action Plan sets out to develop a Wildfire Risk Overlay (map and regulations) in Zoning Bylaw 20001.

The City is to develop a zoning overlay map for Zoning Bylaw 20001 that identifies areas within the wildland urban interface (WUI) where the greatest wildfire risk is present. This map would identify where to apply wildfire risk mitigation zoning regulations to affected properties. The purpose of these zoning regulations is to:

1. Minimize damage and disruption to private and public property in the wildland urban interface due to a wildfire event;
2. Support reducing the cost of rebuilding after a wildfire event; and
3. Ensure the safety of those living in wildfire risk areas.

post.description: Discover tenders, notices and awards; take `reference_number` into `get_posting`. Use `list_codes`, `list_organizations` and `search_unspsc_codes` to find valid filter values.

agreement_types.description: Trade agreement codes from list_codes('trade-agreement'), e.g. TA-01 (not applicable), APC-TA-NWPTA.

categories.description: Category codes from list_codes('opportunity-category'): SRV (services), GD (goods), CNST (construction).

cursor.description: Continuation from a previous call's next_cursor (the 0-based page index). Use the same filters and page_size. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,6}$.

delivery_regions.description: Region of delivery display names (facet values or list_codes('region-of-delivery') display values), e.g. 'Edmonton', 'Alberta'.

include_facets.description: Return facet counts (status, category, organization, region, solicitation/opportunity/agreement type, UNSPSC) for the filtered result set. Organization and UNSPSC facets can be several hundred rows.

opportunity_types.description: Posting type codes from list_codes('opportunity-posting-type'): OPEN-COMPETITIVE, LIMITED, NOTICE, INFORMATIONAL, UNDER-THRESHOLD, LIMITED-UNDER-THRESHOLD.

organizations.description: Contracting organization display names exactly as the site spells them (facet values or list_organizations names), e.g. 'City of Calgary'.

page_size.description:
Rows per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 20.

post_date_from.description: Earliest post date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD, Alberta local date. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

query.description: Free text matched against titles, descriptions and solicitation numbers (e.g. 'wildfire', '935775'). Omit or leave blank to list everything.

query_mode.description:
'standard' is the site's default keyword search; 'enhanced' adds the site's semantic matching (more, looser results).

Provider reference: allowed values ["standard", "enhanced"]; default "standard".

solicitation_types.description: Solicitation type codes from list_codes('opportunity-solicitation-type'): RFP, ITB, RFQ, NRFP, NOA, ACAN, RFEI, NOI, NOS, NPP, SOW, PQR, RFQual, APC-NA.

sort_by.description:
Sort field (the only two the site offers).

Provider reference: allowed values ["post_date", "close_date"]; default "post_date".

sort_direction.description:
sort_direction

Provider reference: allowed values ["asc", "desc"]; default "desc".

statuses.description: Status codes from list_codes('opportunity-status'): OPEN, CLOSED, EVALUATION, SELECTION, AWARD, CANCELLED, UNAWARDABLE, EXPIRED.

unspsc_codes.description: 8-digit UNSPSC codes as strings (segment, family, class or commodity level), e.g. '77000000'. See search_unspsc_codes.

postings.project_description:
The Jackfish Lake Wildfire, Fire Number LCU-003-2023 was approximately 2,553 ha in size.  The wildfire started on May 3rd, 2023, in Athabasca County.  The wildfire encompassed a composite of crown land, private land, grazing leases and forest grazing leases, both within the Forest Protection Area (FPA) and outside the Forest Protection Area (FPA). 

Athabasca County, in its mandate to prevent and suppress wildfires within the County is required to reclaim disturbed forest land caused by wildfire suppression operations. These sites were essential for effective wildfire operations and included fireguards, creek crossings, pipeline crossings, and helipads. Wildfire reclamation is required to prevent or reduce the potential of soil erosion and ensure soil stabilization on or near the fire line. Reclamation of disturbances also promotes the recovery of the disturbed land base for wildlife habitat and vegetative growth. 

The reclamation plan includes the portion of the Jackfish Lake wildfire that is outside the Forest Protection Area (FPA).  The Alberta Government has conducted reclamation activities in the portion of the wildfire withing the Forest Protection Area (FPA).  

Reclamation with mechanical equipment is required to recover the land base to a near natural state. The fireguard travels through trembling aspen and balsam poplar.  White spruce and black spruce are the major coniferous species, with minor compositions tamarack and jack pine, taking advantage of natural clearings when possible. 

The majority of the dozer guards are in higher ground(upland), these areas can be reclaimed in non-frozen dry conditions.  There are stretches of dozer guard classified as upland that may require frozen conditions for access.
postings.title: Athabasca County - Request for Proposal - Jackfish Lake Wildfire Reclamation LCU-003-2023

postings.project_description:
For the primary purpose of wildfire suppression, the Province requires the services of a multiplane Amphibious Airtanker Group supported by one (1) Birddog aircraft. The airtanker group will consist of:

•	A combined Amphibious Airtanker Group capacity of equal to or greater than 10,000 litres with a minimum of two (2) and up to four (4) purposed designed Amphibious Airtankers;  
•	A minimum capacity per Amphibious Airtanker of 3,000 litres;  
•	Each Amphibious Airtanker must be equipped with a compartmentalized or variable/constant flow tank; and 
•	One (1) turbine powered birddog aircraft
All Aircraft must be supported by a fully qualified Aircrew. 
The Province recognizes that there may not be sufficient lead time to acquire, equip, and staff aircraft for the commencement of the 2027 wildfire season. Under these circumstances, the Province may accept the use of one or more Transition Aircraft for a short term, provided the Transition Aircraft are acceptable to the Province. A proposal that includes the use of any Transition Aircraft must be outlined in Attachment #2.

Proponents will supply only aircraft approved by Transport Canada through the issuance of a Canadian Type Certificate or acceptance by Transport Canada of the foreign certificate without issuing its own certificate. Aircraft proposed must meet all Transport Canada legal and regulatory requirements necessary to provide the required Airtanker Services. 

The Contractor will hold a valid license governed by and compliant with the Canadian Transportation Act and a valid Air Operator Certificate (AOC) issued by Transport Canada appropriate to their airtanker operations.

The Province will guarantee 120 days for each Aircraft in each year of the ten year term of the Contract.. There are no guaranteed flying hours during the Core Period.

The Aircraft will be positioned as required throughout Alberta and may be exported outside of the province if required. The Aircraft may be repositioned with minimal notice and for indefinite periods of time.

postings.project_description:
Government of Alberta (GoA) Ministries and Agencies are interested in a broad range of satellite imagery and derivative product offerings. This RFP follows several individual pilot projects, including the use of PlanetScope imagery for Machine Learning (ML) derived wetland inventory in collaboration with Ducks Unlimited Canada (DUC) and the Alberta Biodiversity and Monitoring Institute (ABMI), assessment of very-high resolution satellite ortho and stereo images from a variety of sources to seek opportunities for process improvement and optimization related to forestry operations, forest health, and natural resource management, and a Request for Information (RFI) related to products and services of interest to assist with wildfire preparedness and response. 

The RFP will describe known products and services of potential interest to GoA Department or Agency business areas as well as business requirements where access to satellite imagery, satellite derivative products, or processing infrastructure may provide opportunities or solutions. This RFP will be used to secure one (1) or more price-list contracts with commercial satellite imagery vendors, and/or forestry or remote sensing consultants who best fit the stated needs. The contracts will be used on an as-needed and as-funded basis for pilot projects, or to augment operational capabilities, with no minimum work guarantee. The number of contracts to be signed will be at the sole discretion of the Province.
postings.question_submission_details:
Unless otherwise advised by the Contracting Manager, all questions and any form of communication between the Proponents and the Province in relation to this RFP must be submitted in writing to the Contracting Manager using the following email address: epa.pgccontracts@gov.ab.ca. All questions and responses will be documented.

The Proponent has the responsibility to notify the Province, in writing, of any ambiguity, divergence, error, omission, oversight, contradiction, or item subject to more than one interpretation in this RFP, as it is discovered, and to request any instruction, decision, or direction necessary to prepare the Proposal.

Questions or concerns must be communicated in writing to the Contracting Manager at least three (3) Business Days prior to the RFP’s Closing Date and Time.  Questions received after this time will be answered if, in the opinion of the Province, time permits.

Verbal responses to enquiries are not binding on any party.

Proposals must be submitted electronically, via email, in Microsoft Word or Adobe Acrobat format by the RFP Closing Date and Time to the following email address: epa.pgccontracts@gov.ab.ca.  The email subject line should indicate that it is a Proposal and include the RFP number and title.

The complete Proposal should be in one (1) email, including attachments, and should not be larger than 25MB to facilitate receipt by the Province.  If multiple emails are required to accommodate attachment sizes, the emails should provide clear instructions on how the Proposal is to be integrated (e.g. 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 3 of 3).

The official time and date of receipt of the Proposal will be determined by the email received time as recorded by the Government of Alberta’s email server.  Proponents should be aware that, prior to such electronic delivery, incoming emails are subject to consistency checks and antivirus scans, which process can take several minutes or longer to complete.  The Province will not be responsible for failures (technical or otherwise) that may result in a Proposal not being received prior to the RFP Closing Date and Time.
If the Proposal cannot be opened after reasonable efforts are made by the Province, the Proposal will be rejected.

The Proposal should be secured against accidental modification by the Province while being searchable and printable in its entirety.

Proposals must be received before 14:01:00 Alberta Time on the RFP Closing Date, or the Proposal will be rejected.

Proposals received after the RFP Closing Date and Time will be deleted.

post.description: Find PDB entries for a protein, gene product, organism, ligand or method; join from UniProt with `uniprot_accession` or from a drug with `ligand`. Then call `structure` for chains, ligands, citation and download links.

experimental_method.description:
Combined experimental method label.

Provider reference: allowed values ["X-ray", "EM", "NMR", "Neutron", "Multiple methods", "Integrative", "Other"].

ligand.description: Structures containing this Chemical Component Dictionary id as a non-polymer ligand, e.g. `STI` (imatinib), `HEM`, `ATP`. Look ids up with the `ligand` function. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}$.

limit.description:
limit

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50; default 10.

max_resolution.description:
Best resolution cutoff in ångströms (≤). Entries without a resolution (most NMR) are excluded when set.

Provider reference: maximum 100.

offset.description:
Number of hits to skip; pass the previous page's `next_offset`.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 1000000; default 0.

organism.description: Source organism scientific name, matched case-insensitively against the NCBI taxonomy lineage of every polymer entity, so `Escherichia coli` includes its strains and `Mammalia` includes every mammal.

query.description: Full-text search over titles, descriptions, keywords, organisms, ligand names, citations and annotations, e.g. `imatinib`, `spike glycoprotein`, `CRISPR Cas9`.

released_after.description: Initial release on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

released_before.description: Initial release on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

sort.description:
`relevance` (search score), `newest` (initial release date, newest first) or `resolution` (best first, entries without a resolution last).

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "newest", "resolution"]; default "relevance".

uniprot_accession.description: Structures with a polymer entity mapped to this UniProtKB accession (SIFTS/RCSB reference sequence mapping), e.g. `P69905` for human hemoglobin alpha. Pattern: ^([OPQopq][0-9][A-Za-z0-9]{3}[0-9]|[A-NR-Za-nr-z][0-9]([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{2}[0-9]){1,2})$.

200.description:
Search Rover sitters for one service around a location (`GET /api/v7/search-optimized/`, endpoint ep-search-api). Filters: `service_type` (overnight-boarding = boarding in the sitter's home, overnight-traveling = house sitting in the owner's home, drop-in = drop-in visits, dog-walking, doggy-day-care), `location` as a free-text place (use the exact `description` from `suggest_locations`, e.g. `Seattle, WA, USA`), `pet_type` dog or cat, optional `start_date`/`end_date`, dog-size flags, `min_price`/`max_price` and `page` (20 results per page; `next_page` and the continuation give the next one). Each result is a sitter card: opk and slug (the identifiers `get_sitter`, `get_sitter_availability` and `list_sitter_reviews` take), name, headline, listed price per unit in the market currency, rating and review counts, neighbourhood and distance from the search centre, badges, and `available_for_selected_dates` exactly as Rover reports it (`unknown` is a real value: search results never confirm availability; use `get_sitter_availability`). The response `location` block says what Rover geocoded the input to. A location Rover cannot geocode makes it fall back to the request IP's area; this program refuses that with `invalid_input` instead of returning unrelated sitters. Market follows the proxy exit (US, USD); a non-US location therefore also fails as not resolvable.

Filters: `service_type` (overnight-boarding = boarding in the sitter's home, overnight-traveling = house sitting in the owner's home, drop-in = drop-in visits, dog-walking, doggy-day-care), `location` as a free-text place (use the exact `description` from `suggest_locations`, e.g. `Seattle, WA, USA`), `pet_type` dog or cat, optional `start_date`/`end_date`, dog-size flags, `min_price`/`max_price` and `page` (20 results per page; `next_page` and the continuation give the next one). Each result is a sitter card: opk and slug (the identifiers `get_sitter`, `get_sitter_availability` and `list_sitter_reviews` take), name, headline, listed price per unit in the market currency, rating and review counts, neighbourhood and distance from the search centre, badges, and `available_for_selected_dates` exactly as Rover reports it (`unknown` is a real value: search results never confirm availability; use `get_sitter_availability`). The response `location` block says what Rover geocoded the input to. A location Rover cannot geocode makes it fall back to the request IP's area; this program refuses that with `invalid_input` instead of returning unrelated sitters. Market follows the proxy exit (US, USD); a non-US location therefore also fails as not resolvable.

200.description:
Observations of one dataflow selected by country, other dimension codes and period, as records. Give `filters` (dimension id to code(s); REF_AREA is the country) or a raw `key`, plus optional start_period/end_period. Unknown dimensions or codes without data fail with invalid_input listing the valid ones; a combination with no data is not_found. Selections above 50,000 observations are rejected: add filters or a period range. One data download per page (OECD allows about 60 per hour); rows are sorted canonically and the cursor pins the dataflow version and segment hash, so a publication change fails with upstream_error `publication_changed` instead of mixing data. Each record carries every dimension and attribute code, obs_value, time_period, series_key, source_record_id and source_url; Revenue Statistics and financial market rows also get a typed `mapped` view. filters.description: Codes per dimension id, e.g. {"REF_AREA": "USA", "FREQ": "Q", "TRADE_FLOW": ["X", "M"]}. Countries go in REF_AREA as ISO3 codes; dimensions left out are wildcards. structure_get lists the dimension ids and the codes with data. Use instead of `key`.

include_hash.description: Download the CSV segment and return its canonical SHA-256 and size. Costs one data download; the segment must be under 50,000 observations.

key.description: Raw SDMX series key in dimension order (see structure_get); empty position = wildcard, `+` joins codes. Prefer `filters`, which cannot get the positions wrong. Pattern: ^(all|[A-Za-z0-9_@+.-]*)$.

value.text:
The total value of investment in building construction edged up $25.1 million (+0.1%) to $23.5 billion in August. An increase in the non-residential sector (+1.0%) was moderated by a slight decline in the residential sector (-0.3%). Year over year, investment in building construction grew 7.9% in August.

On a constant dollar basis (2023=100), the total value of investment in building construction edged down 0.1% from the previous month to $21.2 billion in August, but it was up 4.7% year over year.

## Institutional and commercial components drive growth in non-residential investment

In August, the value of investment in non-residential building construction increased $70.5 million to $7.4 billion. Both the institutional (+1.9%) and commercial (+0.8%) components contributed to the increase, while the industrial component (-0.1%) showed little change.

Investment in institutional construction rose $43.5 million to $2.4 billion in August. Gains in Ontario (+$35.9 million) and Quebec (+$15.3 million) were moderated by declines in British Columbia (-$4.6 million) and Alberta (-$3.1 million). Investment in schools and education building construction led to the increase in the institutional component, driven by major projects in the Toronto and Montréal census metropolitan areas.

Investment in commercial construction grew $27.9 million to $3.6 billion in August. Ontario (+$18.5 million) and Quebec (+$8.0 million) were the primary contributors to the increase.

Meanwhile, investment in industrial construction edged down $0.8 million to $1.5 billion in August. This modest change was largely attributable to Quebec (-$6.6 million), Alberta (-$3.8 million) and Ontario (-$3.0 million). The gain in British Columbia (+$12.5 million) partially offset the overall decline.

## Investment in residential construction edges down

In August, investment in residential building construction edged down $45.4 million to $16.1 billion. The single-family component (-1.3%) led the slight decline, while the multi-unit component increased 0.6%.

Investment in single-family home construction was down $98.3 million to $7.6 billion in August. British Columbia (-$46.5 million) and Quebec (-$45.7 million) drove the decrease and were supported by declines across four other provinces and two territories.

Meanwhile, investment in multi-unit construction rose $52.9 million to $8.5 billion in August. Gains in Quebec (+$74.7 million) and British Columbia (+$65.2 million) were partially offset by declines in five provinces and one territory, led by Ontario (-$79.4 million).

For more information on construction, please visit the Construction statistics portal.

For more information on housing, please visit the Housing statistics portal.

## Note to readers

This content was created with the assistance of a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool and refined and verified by Statistics Canada experts. To learn more about how the agency uses AI responsibly, please visit the Trust Centre.

Table 34-10-0286 has been archived on the Statistics Canada website and will no longer be updated but may still be viewed. The successor table is 34-10-0293, and the information from January 2017 onwards that was in table 34-10-0286 is still available in the new table, except for the constant dollar series, which has been rebased to 2023=100. Constant dollar data for January and February 2017 represent an average between the old base year (2012=100) and the new base year (2023=100) and should be used with caution. The 2017 data series will be backcasted and the figures will be revised with the release of our annual revision.

Data are subject to revisions based on late responses, delayed construction start dates for large projects, methodological changes, classification updates, price index updates for constant dollar series, benchmarking and adjustments to ad hoc macroeconomic events. Unadjusted data have been revised back to 2021. Seasonally adjusted data have been revised back to 2018.

Data presented in this release are seasonally adjusted with current dollar values unless otherwise stated. Using seasonally adjusted data allows month-to-month and quarter-to-quarter comparisons by removing the effects of seasonal variations. For information on seasonal adjustment, see the page Seasonal adjustment: Concepts and interpretation, 2026.

Monthly estimates for constant dollars are calculated using quarterly deflators from the Building Construction Price Index (18-10-0289-01). The monthly indexes used for the deflation process were part of a methodology review to increase the quality of the constant dollar and seasonally adjusted series. The indexes previously displayed a step pattern because of less frequent collection.

Detailed data on investment activity by type of building and type of work are now available in the unadjusted current dollar series.

The trade and services subcomponent includes buildings such as retail and wholesale outlets, retail complexes and motor vehicle show rooms. More detailed information can be found on the Integrated Metadatabase at Types of Building Structure - 2.2.1 - Trade and services.

## Next release

Data on investment in building construction for September will be released on November 19.

## Contact information

For more information, or to enquire about the concepts, methods or data quality of this release, contact us (toll-free 1-800-263-1136; 514-283-8300; infostats@statcan.gc.ca) or Media Relations (statcan.mediahotline-ligneinfomedias.statcan@statcan.gc.ca).

value.description:
Questacon requires a permanent adjustable lighting and projection rig for Gallery 8, the Drum. The purpose of the rig is to expand lighting capability for a wide variety of future exhibition installations in the space. This will include improved lighting for items anywhere on the on the gallery floor as well as suspended in the large void above. The rig will enable the creation of dynamic lighting, projection, and visual effects particularly overhead in the tall gallery void. Together with existing hanging points, the rig will provide the ability to suspend large objects in the void ranging from sculptural artwork pieces to fabrics, scrims or string curtains for large scale projection effects.
Questacon has developed a rig concept that features a 12m diameter box truss ring called the Halo - see concept drawings. This truss will require new suspension points from the existing structural steel work above the Gallery 8 ceiling. The Halo will be able to be raised or lowered to adjust the display height for a particular exhibition as well as allow for installation, cleaning, and maintenance from the gallery floor. The truss is to be black to disappear into the dark void and the suspension cables should be visually minimal. Winches, motors and other equipment will be hidden above the gallery ceiling while a control interface should be provided in an accessible location from the gallery floor whilst not adding any visual clutter to the exhibition space. The truss will need power for lighting and projection equipment, lighting and projection protocols, as well as data. A reticulation system above the gallery ceiling is required for minimal and discrete power and data cable management.
An 8.5 metre diameter black circular box truss, is also envisioned for the space, suspended from existing cleats or pulley cleats. This will provide multiple customisable rigging points for objects suspended in the space, sail tracking around the perimeter to hang scrims or string curtains, and can also carry lighting and projectors on droppers or risers. This truss will be raised and lowered independently of the Halo, and will need its own power and data cable system, as well as a control system. Again, equipment is to be hidden above the ceiling to minimise visual impact.
value.other_instructions: All personal on site must hold a valid Working with Vulnerable People card or state equivalent.

values.name: 0 - VIN decoded clean. Check Digit (9th position) is correct
1 - Check Digit (9th position) does not calculate properly
2 - VIN corrected, error in one position
3 - VIN corrected, error in one position (assuming Check Digit is correct)
4 - VIN corrected, error in one position only (indicated by ! in Suggested VIN), multiple matches found
5 - VIN has errors in few positions
7 - Manufacturer is not registered with NHTSA for sale or importation in the U.S. for use on U.S roads; Please contact the manufacturer directly for more information
9 - Glider Warning - A "Glider" is not a "motor vehicle", as defined in 49 U.S.C. 30102(a)(6), and cannot be assigned a VIN that meets 49 CFR Part 565 requirements

10 - Off-Road Vehicle Warning – This is not a Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) for a motor vehicle. This indicates that the manufacturer did not certify this product as complying with the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards that are applicable to motor vehicles as defined in 49 U.S.C. 30102.
11 - Incorrect Model Year - Position 10 does not match valid model year codes (I, O, Q, U, Z, 0). Decoded data may not be accurate.
12 - Model Year Warning - Model Year entered for decoding with VIN does not match the model year based on the 10th position in VIN.
14 - Unable to provide information for some of the characters in the VIN, based on the manufacturer submission.

geometry.description: GeoJSON (RFC 7946, WGS84, [lon, lat]) Point, Polygon, MultiPolygon, or a Feature wrapping one. Rings must be closed; altitude is ignored; a FeatureCollection is refused (send one place per call); geometries crossing the antimeridian are refused; at most 500 vertices and 250 km2. Any other member (bbox, Feature properties, id) passes through unread. Invalid input is reported as invalid_input with a JSON pointer and a stable code: missing_type, unsupported_type, feature_collection, missing_coordinates, not_a_position, latitude (with a swapped-order hint), longitude, ring_too_short, ring_not_closed, too_many_vertices, too_large, antimeridian, outside_coverage.

include_boundaries.description: Also look up the intersecting county, community and tribal area polygons (three FeatureServer queries). Default true.

layers.description: Image service layers to read. Default: burn_probability, risk_to_potential_structures, conditional_risk_to_potential_structures, wildfire_hazard_potential, exposure_type.

200.description:
Wildfire risk for a GeoJSON geometry (Point, Polygon, MultiPolygon or a Feature wrapping one; WGS84 [lon, lat]). For a Point, the 30 m pixel of each requested USFS image service layer is read (identify); for a polygon, zonal statistics over the rings (computeStatisticsHistograms: pixel count, min, max, mean, median, mode, class fractions). Values are returned both as the service pixel value and scaled to the published quantity with the attribute-table class name. Also returns the county, community and tribal area polygons the geometry intersects with their housing counts and percentile ranks, a location echo, sources and missing[] entries for layers without data. Outside CONUS/Alaska/Hawaii is invalid_input with code outside_coverage.

value.description_html:
The central bank in Europe is called the European Central Bank (ECB). Currently, 17 EU member states have adopted the Euro. It is the second-most traded currency on the forex market, after the US Dollar, and also a major global reserve currency. Other common names for the Euro include Yoyo (Irish English), Leru (Spanish), and Ege (Finnish).

Introduction of the Euro
On January 1, 1999, the Euro (EUR) was introduced as an account currency, replacing the European Currency Unit at par. The European Currency Unit was a theoretical basket of currencies rather than a physical currency in and of itself. Initially, eleven of the countries in the European Economic and Monetary Union replaced their own currencies with the Euro: Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain. Greece followed suit in 2001, Slovenia in 2007, Malta and Cyprus in 2008, Slovakia in 2009 and Latvia in 2014.

Use of the Euro outside the EU
A number of sovereign states that are not part of the European Union have since adopted the Euro, including the Principality of Andorra, the Principality of Monaco, the Republic of San Marino, and the Vatican City. The Euro is also used in many territories, departments, and sovereign states of Euro-zone countries, such as the Azores, Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Europa Island, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Juan de Nova, the Madeira Islands, Martinique, Mayotte, Reunion, Saint-Martin, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, to name just a few. The Euro is used as a trading currency in Cuba, North Korea, and Syria and several currencies are pegged to it.

Value of Obsolete National Currencies
Euro bank notes and coins began circulating in 2002 with old notes and coins gradually being withdrawn from circulation. The precise dates that each old currency ceased being legal tender and their official fixed rates are shown in the table below.

The XE Currency Converter supports the above obsolete currencies; to make a conversion, type the name of the currency in the search box. Some old currencies are still physically convertible at special locations. For details, refer to the official ECB site listed in the Relevant Links section below.

Spelling and Capitalization
The official spelling of the EUR currency unit is "euro", with a lower case "e"; however, the common industry practice is to spell it "Euro", with a capital "E". Many languages have different official spellings for the Euro, which also may or may not coincide with general use. Additionally, there are various nicknames for the currency including, Ege (Finnish), Pavo (Spanish), and Euráče (Slovak).

Relevant Links
For more information on the EUR, we encourage you to visit the links below, particularly the European Central Bank. These sites include recent news on the Euro as well as issues like implementation, spelling, legislation, and more.
